- writing-migration-plans: How to order the phases of an implementation or migration plan so nothing stalls mid-run — front-load the out-of-band setup, collapse the review gates into one stacked-PR pass, leave only executable steps — and how to keep its tracking issue append-only while implementing. Use when writing or reviewing a migration plan or a phased implementation plan, and when working through one's tracking issue.
- writing-tasks: The contract a Claudinite task is written to — the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the precondition as the only decision point, ordering, and how a work item converges. Use when writing or changing a tasks/<name>/task.mjs or its worker, or when a task-declaration check fires.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.
- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
- docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.
- morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.

{"number":1003,"title":"Manual: register this fleet owner's GitHub App and deploy its token exchange","body":"Four steps no Action can take — they need a credential and a console. Until all four are done the dashboard runs **unauthenticated at 60 requests/hour per IP**, which one fleet sweep exceeds. Context in #996.

**Scope: once per fleet *owner*, not once per fleet — and not once for everybody.** One App and one exchange endpoint serve every deployment *you* own. A GitHub App carries [up to 10 callback URLs](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/about-the-user-authorization-callback-url), and with **wildcard matching** a single callback of `https://.github.io/` covers every project Pages site under that host — so a new Shepherd for a new fleet of yours adds no callback at all, just the two config keys.

Somebody else adopting this pack cannot inherit it, for mechanical reasons: a private App "can only be installed on the account that owns the app. Only members of the organization that owns it can authorize it", and even a public one yields a user token that "can only access resources that both the user and app can access" — so until they install it themselves their whole fleet reads *not visible to you*, and their tokens would be minted by someone else's endpoint. They register their own, or use the token box. Spelled out in the pack README (#1007).

- [ ] **Register a GitHub App** ([new App](https://github.com/settings/apps/new)) with read-only **Contents**, **Issues** and **Actions**, and *Request user authorization (OAuth) during installation* enabled. Callback URL: the deployed dashboard's page URL — or the `https://.github.io/` root with **Enable wildcard matching** ticked, which covers every future deployment on that host. Note the **client ID**, generate a **client secret**.
  - *while undone:* no sign-in button exists; every viewer is anonymous.
- [ ] **Install the App** on the account holding the fleet's repos ([installations](https://github.com/settings/installations)). Once per *account*, not per repo — a new repo under an installed account is covered by "all repositories", or added to the selection.
  - *while undone:* sign-in succeeds but the token can read nothing, so every member row reads "not visible to you".
- [ ] **Deploy the exchange** — [`oauth-exchange.example.mjs`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/packs/claudinite-dashboard/oauth-exchange.example.mjs) as-is to a worker, with the client ID and secret as its environment. One deployment serves every dashboard you own, since it holds that App's secret and nothing else.
  - *while undone:* clicking sign-in returns to a page that cannot finish, and says the exchange was unreachable.
- [ ] **Set `clientId` and `exchangeUrl`** on the deployment's `claudinite-dashboard` entry in its `.claudinite-checks.json`. Either alone does nothing — the pair is what turns sign-in on. This is the one step a new fleet of yours repeats, with the same two values.
  - *while undone:* nothing changes; the page keeps falling back to the token box.

**Closing condition:** the deployed dashboard shows *Sign in with GitHub*, one authorization gets a viewer through a full fleet sweep, and the rate pill reads `…/5000 · user`.

### Why the exchange cannot be skipped

Verified against the [authorizing-OAuth-apps docs](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/oauth-apps/building-oauth-apps/authorizing-oauth-apps):

- the web flow's token exchange lists `client_secret` as **Required**, flatly — GitHub supports PKCE (`code_challenge`, S256 only) but as *additional* protection, not as a public-client mode that drops the secret;
- the device flow genuinely needs no secret ("The `client_secret` is not needed for the device flow") but it POSTs to `github.com/login/device/code` and `github.com/login/oauth/access_token`, and those are cross-origin for a page on `github.io`. The docs state "CORS pre-flight requests (OPTIONS) are not supported at this time"; a browser cannot read a response that carries no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` either. *(The response headers of the token endpoint could not be probed from this sandbox — the proxy denies it — so that last half is documented, not measured here.)*

A browser extension is the case where this *does* work without a server, which is why the Chrome extension flow felt server-free: an extension with host permissions is not subject to the page's CORS rules, so it can call the token endpoint itself. A static page has no such exemption.

This is not a wider credential in each member repo — the App acts as whoever signed in, with exactly their own permissions.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1003","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-18T14:14:11Z","updated_at":"2026-08-18T15:02:49Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":994,"title":"usage-fold's `tasks` census has no writer under the queue","body":"Fallout from #974, found while re-evaluating the docs against the new model.

The `tasks` rows in `.claudinite/local/usage.GENERATED.json` were a **census** of scheduled work — every due task counted, captured or not — read from the `claudinite-task-run v1 …` lines the slot scheduler printed into its own Actions log. #974 deleted that writer. The parser stays (logs inside Actions retention are still real), so the rows keep counting until that window ages out and then count nothing.

`taskExec` is unaffected: it comes from captured sessions, and #993 restored the capture step the queue's instructions had lost.

What the queue has instead is better and is a different read: **each occurrence's outcome is a label on its own work item** — `outcome:done`, `outcome:delivered`, `outcome:obsolete`, `needs-human` — queryable by search rather than by downloading job logs, and durable past Actions retention.

So this is a new read, not a repair:

- [ ] count closed `[claudinite-work]` items per `pack/task` per day by their `outcome:*` label
- [ ] decide whether it still needs the `runsFoldedThrough` append-once watermark — the reason for it was the REST cost of job logs, and an issue search is much cheaper, so the rows may simply become recomputable like every other family
- [ ] retire `parseTaskRun`/`TASK_RUN_OUTCOMES` and `read-task-runs.mjs` once the last slot-era logs are past retention

`packs/grow_with_claudinite/tasks/usage-fold/task.md` states the gap as it stands, so nobody reads the rows as current.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/994","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-18T09:52:13Z","updated_at":"2026-08-18T09:52:13Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":991,"title":"Promote conformance-work-scope to blocking once the fleet carries the step","body":"#977 landed `conformance-work-scope` (core) as **advisory**, deliberately: a requirement added to the canon with no path for consumers to comply first is the #555 failure, and its sibling `conformance-workflow` is staged the same way. This issue is the mechanism that brings the promotion back rather than leaving it to memory.

## The closing condition

Every member's CI runs the work sweep — i.e. no member's world sweep reports `conformance-work-scope`. Read it off the fleet rather than off memory:

- each member's own sweep output (the advisory finding is the signal), or
- each member's workflows containing `engine/checks/ci-work-scope.mjs`.

Delivery is by the nightly converge (owner decision, 2026-08-18 — not forced): the engine file ships with the engine tree, and the `core` bump 3 → 4 ships the check. So members cannot begin complying until their next converge, and the advisory finding is what tells each one what to add.

## The promotion itself

One line in [`packs/core/conformance-work-scope.mjs`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/packs/core/conformance-work-scope.mjs) — `severity: 'advisory'` → `'blocking'` — plus the catalog row in `packs/core/README.md` and a `core` version bump.

**Do not promote while any member is still missing the step.** A blocking finding reds that member's next maintenance PR, and since delivery arms auto-merge — a queue for checks — a red check there does not annoy anyone: it stops the repo updating, quietly. That is #939's failure mode from the other direction.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/991","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-18T08:46:55Z","updated_at":"2026-08-18T08:46:55Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

[{"id":5304690136,"body":"Owner decision (2026-08-15, DESIGN §15.22): **`maxItems` defaults to one** — one run settles one item, serially, and a run ending with items still pickable re-dispatches a fresh run via `workflow_dispatch`. Two additions to this issue's scope:

[{"id":5316661692,"body":"Two more findings from the same adoption, on the owner's instruction to keep them here rather than open separate issues. Both are about **how a human-handover step is written**, so they sit one level up from the path bug above — that one is a wrong address, these are a wrong shape.

## 1. A GitHub settings step must be a deep link, not a breadcrumb trail

The handover issue this adoption produced said things like:

> Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret

Every one of those is a URL the agent already knows how to construct — it has the `owner/repo` — so making the human navigate is pure friction, and a breadcrumb goes stale the moment GitHub reorganizes a settings page while a URL keeps redirecting. The rule the owner asked for: **hyperlink every requested GitHub setting change, to the deepest page that exists.**

The patterns worth naming wherever this lands:

| Step | URL |
|---|---|
| New Actions secret | `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/settings/secrets/actions/new` |
| Actions secrets and variables | `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/settings/secrets/actions` |
| Workflow permissions, Actions general | `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/settings/actions` |
| Auto-merge, merge methods, general | `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/settings` |
| Branch protection / rulesets | `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/settings/branches` |
| Environments | `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/settings/environments` |

This is general to every repo the fleet adopts, not specific to the one that hit it — which is why it is here and not in that repo's local pack.

## 2. Don't ask a human to enable something GitHub enables by default

The same issue carried a checkbox for **Settings → General → "Allow squash merging"**, on the reasoning that the merge recipe squashes always. But GitHub enables all three merge methods on a new repository, so the box could only ever be already-ticked. A handover list whose items are mostly no-ops teaches the reader to skim it, which is exactly the failure mode a handover list exists to prevent.

Worth stating as a rule where the handover shape is defined: **a handover step must name a change from the platform's default.** If the default already satisfies the requirement, the requirement is met and there is nothing to hand over.

Both corrections are applied in the consuming repo's own issue ([missingbulb/Shepherd#3](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/issues/3)) — this is the upstream half, so the next adoption does not repeat either.

One consequence of keeping all three here: this issue's title now names only the first finding. Worth retitling to something like *"bootstrap.md Part 9 path bug, plus two rules for writing human-handover steps"* if it is going to be triaged by title.

{"number":801,"title":"Migration to the work-item queue: two PRs, one same-day validation burst","body":"The phase plan for [tasks-dispatch DESIGN](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md) (§14 points here). Design constraints from the owner (2026-08-13): **fewest disparate steps, fewest approval points, and certainty the same day** — we do not wait for a nightly run to learn whether the end state works. Deliberately generating real work to push traffic through every path is explicitly sanctioned.

**Approval points: two.** PR‑1 (mechanism + canon flip) and PR‑2 (fleet flip + slot deletion). Everything else is forcing and observing, which the mechanism itself defines as ordinary operations.

Checkboxes track progress; each burst row's checkbox is checked only with an evidence URL appended beside it.

---

## Where this stands (2026-08-16 12:10Z)

**One member is verified end to end, agentic lane included. Twelve more are blocked on owner-only credential work.** Steps 0–2 complete. Step 3 is most of the way: the flip is merged and observed, the first member ran a real agentic item to `outcome:done`, and three defects the burst could not have caught were found and two fixed. The slot deletion still waits on the remaining members.

| | state |
|---|---|
| Canon | on the queue since #854; 12 clean scheduler runs overnight, 12 items to terminal state |
| Fleet | flipped by default in #888 (`17902b9`); **GCEC verified end to end**, 12 members still need a CCR routine (#916) |
| Slot machinery | still in the tree, deliberately — deleting it before members are verified strands them (see Step 3) |
| Design vs engine | DESIGN/sim current to §15.24 plus F24; engine at pre-review behavior — the catch-up is Step 4 (#883) |
| Open follow-ups | #916 (owner-only, blocking), #921, #892, #924, #883, #877 |

## Step 0 — rehearsal (done)

- [x] Simulator + scenario suite green in CI; coverage map names the live-only rows

## Step 1 — PR‑1 on canon: the whole mechanism, canon flipped (approval №1)

- [x] Label vocabulary, tick workflow (cron + `workflow_dispatch`), executor workflow, janitor re-target, dependency fields + `after` yield + `create-work-item`, F8 signal exclusions, canon flipped, gate green
- [x] **Approval №1: PR‑1 merged** — #854, `b30ef77`

## Step 2 — the validation burst (complete)

- [x] **B1 creation + first-item rule (S25):** [run 31899008771](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31899008771) — 12 items #860–#870, each `task:blocked` wearing its next anchor
- [x] **B2 the roll + reasons on record (S1′):** #860 — one ask, rolled to tomorrow, reason on the item, no comment spam
- [x] **B3 agentic happy path + real CCR invocation + records (S2):** #867 — wake → claim → hand-off with nonce → **live session in 31s** → result + exec record → `outcome:done`
- [x] **B4 agentless path end to end:** #859 — wake → executor in 2s → claim → prework → `outcome:done`, closed in 26s, no session
- [x] **B5 the chain + yield (S4/S23):** #863 — yielded while `core/update` was live ([run 31913047785](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31913047785)), then claimed and running the moment the upstream cleared; its work merged as #887
- [x] ~~**B6 hourly cadence**~~ — **dropped** (owner). `create-extractor` is `gcec/create-extractor` on GoogleCalendarEventCreator, the fleet's only hourly task; canon has none
- [x] ~~**B7 missing-secret posture**~~ — **folded into Step 3** (owner): every member reaches the flip with its endpoint token unset, so the posture happens on real traffic with no scaffolding
- [x] **B8 force-while-executing mutex (S15):** #871 — queued behind the executing twin, then got its own verdict on release
- [x] **B9 multi-executor lease (S7):** #873 — three overlapping executors, exactly one claim, one execution
- [x] **B10 follow-up fields (S17):** #872 — `Blocked-by` + `Not-before` created and held blocked by the tick
- [x] **B11 janitor leashes:** [run 31900490000](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31900490000) — 12 blocked/rolling items, zero escalations
- [x] **All burst rows green**

### What the burst caught that the rehearsal could not

Four defects, none of which any simulator would have produced. Three are fixed:

- **#879 → #881 (merged).** Hand-off appended a second `### Context` instead of replacing the first, splitting the item's binding scope while `instructions.md` says to read "the Context section", singular. Every unit test passed, because each tested one call. Confirmed fixed on live traffic in B5's own hand-off.
- **#882 → #885 (merged).** Queue sessions wrote `[unknown]` where the exec record's slot id used to go — `instructions.md` never said what replaces it — dropping the join from a record back to its work item.
- **The task-path guard fired correctly** on a hand-built item naming `task.mjs` instead of `task.md` (#871): refused, converged to `needs-human`, nothing run.
- **#892 (open).** The terminal convergence is agent-discretion, and **both** agentic runs got part of it wrong — #867's record field, and #863 closing with no outcome label and no exec record at all. Proposes a `converge-item.mjs` the session calls with its judged outcome.

## Step 3 — the fleet flip, then the deletion (approval №2)

**PR‑2 is two PRs, not one** (amendment, 2026-08-15). The plan said "slot machinery deleted in this same PR"; that is unsafe, and the reason is in the code:

- `updates/engine-update.mjs` **replaces the mount wholesale**, so a file canon deletes leaves every member's mount on its next converge whatever that member's config says.
- `.github/workflows/` is the one path a converge cannot push — staged, and landed later by the apply stage.
- The two stubs call **different entry points**: `run.mjs` vs `queue/tick.mjs`.

So deleting slots in the flip's own release strands any member whose workflow has not yet landed. Keeping the slot code makes that window benign (`run.mjs` no-ops) and #888 makes it **loud**.

- [x] The pack update flow staged only the scheduler workflow, so `claudinite-executor.yml` reached no member — #874, `5ca4c35`
- [x] **Approval №2: the flip merged** — #888, `17902b9`. `dispatchMode` answers `queue` for an absent setting, so members flip with **no edit to any file they own**

{"number":1072,"title":"Production code must not reference its tests — land it as a check","body":"Owner decision while landing #1066: **there shouldn't be references to tests from production code.** That change removed the four citations it created; the rule itself is still unwritten, and eleven pre-existing sites still cross the line.

## The rule

A shipping `.mjs` under `packs/` or `engine/` must not name a `*.test.mjs` path. It is deterministic, so it belongs on the ladder as a **check**, not prose — the assurance authored and seen to fail before the sites are cleaned.

Documentation is a separate question and probably outside it: `engine/checks/README.md` describing where a pack's tests live, or `.github/workflows/ci.yml` naming test globs, is the corpus documenting itself, not production code pointing at its own test.

## The sites as of today

```
engine/checks/helpers/active-migrations.mjs:103
engine/pack_loader/pack-schema.mjs:72
engine/scheduler/queue/prework-run.mjs:3
engine/scheduler/run.mjs:10
engine/scheduler/signals/index.mjs:35
engine/scheduler/slots.mjs:18
packs/claudinite-dashboard/model.mjs:11
packs/claudinite-dashboard/tasks/fleet-digest/dated-fixture-collision.mjs:4
packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs:14, :36
packs/claudinite-lifecycle/rules-index-current.mjs:26, :51
```

Most say the same thing — "a guard pins this" — and lose nothing by naming the guard rather than its file, which is how the four in #1066 were resolved.

## Why it is not folded into #1066

Cleaning these touches three more pack directories, so it re-delivers `claudinite-dashboard`, `claudinite-growth` and `claudinite-lifecycle` on their version bumps. That restructure's whole constraint was that members see nothing, so the sweep is its own change.

## Where the check lives

`.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/` if it is a canon-corpus rule, or a shared pack if it should reach members — worth deciding first, since the second choice makes it every member's rule and a much wider first run.

{"number":924,"title":"A losing claimant's own comment bumps updated_at, so contention postpones the leash reclaim it depends on","body":"Split out of #922 at the owner's direction — a latent issue the strike does **not** fix.

The tick's executing-leash reclaim keys on the item's activity clock, which is GitHub's `updated_at`. Every claim attempt posts a comment, and a comment bumps `updated_at` — including the attempt of an executor that goes on to *lose* the arbitration and walk away.

So on an item nobody is actually working, each losing claimant resets the clock the reclaim is counting down. The busier the queue, the more executors arrive, the further the recovery is pushed out. Under a `labeled`-event executor plus an hourly drain, an item can be re-touched often enough that the leash never elapses.

This is what made the observed stall on canon #860 ~10h rather than the ~1h the leash nominally promises: the failed claims kept the item looking alive.

#922 removes the *cause* of those repeated losing claims, so the common case goes away with it. What stays is the general property: whenever an executor genuinely dies mid-claim, any later claim attempt on that item defers its recovery. Contention postpones the mechanism that exists precisely to recover from failure.

Worth considering:
- read the last **heartbeat/claim by the current holder** as the activity clock, rather than the item's `updated_at` — the heartbeat work in #883 already introduces a per-holder liveness signal, which is the natural carrier;
- or have a losing claimant not write to the item at all, which needs a claim protocol that reads before it writes (a bigger change, and it trades away the property that makes the current one correct under a stale snapshot).

Not urgent — the failure needs a dead executor *and* ongoing contention on the same item — but it should not be discovered a second time from a stall.

- [x] **Phase 1 — GCEC pilot:** vendor-refresh, scheduler workflow, strip the release cron, labels, move both `dev/routines/` into the gcec pack as `tasks/`, port the create-extractor triage *decision* into the precondition (fetch/scaffold stay in the task), write the `schedule` key, create the label-wired executor routine, disable the two old GCEC triggers. - [ ] **Phase 4 — decommission:** delete the central CCR trigger + both disabled GCEC triggers; remove `routines/auto-all-repos-maintenance.md` + `routines/fleet/`; drop the transition guard, `run_daily`/`local_packs` aliases; retire enrollment; final boxed review vs DESIGN §8.

{"number":920,"title":"sharedMount's path regex is mount-only, so the signal is dead in the canon home","body":"`engine/scheduler/signals/index.mjs`'s `sharedMount` collector matches vendored pack files as:

```js
/^\.claudinite\/shared\/packs\/([^/]+)\//
```

The canon home runs the same engine from its repo root, where there is no `.claudinite/shared/` and the shared packs are `packs/`. So `changedPacks` is permanently empty here, and every precondition reading it is blind in the one repo whose canon moves every day:

- `grow_with_claudinite/growth-dedup` can only ever wake on its local-packs arm.
- `core/update` loses the "a pack moved" arm of its overdue gate.

The two-root form the local pack's own rule prescribes:

```js
/^(?:\.claudinite\/shared\/)?packs\/([^/]+)\/.+/
```

A local pack (`.claudinite/local/packs/…`, `.claudinite/local_packs/…`) matches neither root, which is the intent.

Split out of #912 / #913, which needed the same discrimination and does it inside the pack (`packs/grow_with_claudinite/tasks/growth-dedup/worker.mjs`'s `canonPackOf`, with its own tests). Landing it engine-side would let that worker read the shared form instead — worth doing, but it is engine work with two consumers, so it gets its own change rather than riding a pack PR.

{"number":892,"title":"The queue's terminal convergence is agent-discretion, and both live runs got part of it wrong","body":"Two agentic runs have now executed on the work-item queue (#801 burst). **Neither converged its item correctly**, in different ways:

| item | task | what it did | what was wrong |
|---|---|---|---|
| [#867](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/867) | `tidy-repo/tidy-issues` | closed, `outcome:done`, `task:agent` dropped, exec record printed | the record's occurrence field said `[unknown]` (#882, fixed in #885) |
| [#863](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/863) | `grow_with_claudinite/growth-extract` | closed as completed, thorough result comment, `verify-outcome.mjs` run | **no `outcome:` label at all**, `task:agent` still on the closed item, and **no `claudinite-task-exec` record whatsoever** |

The #863 session did the *hard* parts impeccably — it opened and merged its PR inside the `merged-pr` ceiling, deduped against 585 lines of existing pack prose, ran the prose-to-checks upgrade pass, verified with `verify-outcome.mjs`, posted to its tracker, and even caught and fixed a false-positive check on its own commit message. It then fumbled the bookkeeping, which is the part that is not judgment at all.

That is the shape of the problem: **the terminal transition is mechanical, and we are asking an agent to perform it from prose.** `instructions.md` step 5 is a table of labels plus "then print the `claudinite-task-exec` record" — five ordered side effects (comment, swap label, add outcome, print record, close) that a session performs by hand at the end of a long run, when its context is fullest and the remaining work looks like formality.

What it costs:

- **The outcome census is unreliable.** Outcome labels are the cross-check on exec records; an item closed with neither is invisible to both.
- **A closed item wearing `task:agent`** reads as live to anything scanning labels, and is a lie the janitor cannot correct — its sweeps are over *open* items.
- Both failures are silent. Nothing fails, nothing is red, and the item looks finished.

### Proposed fix

Give the session a deterministic converge step to call, the way `verify-outcome.mjs` already exists beside it for the ceiling check:

```
node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/queue/converge-item.mjs --issue  --outcome done|delivered|needs-human --summary 
```

The **agent supplies the judgment** — which outcome, and the prose of what happened. The **code performs the transition**: post the comment, swap `task:agent` off, add the outcome label, print the exec record with the item number in it, close with the right `state_reason`. Same split as everywhere else in this engine (`executor.mjs`: "the pure decisions live at the top… the shell below is the I/O"), and the executor already has all five operations written for the paths it converges itself.

`instructions.md` step 5 then becomes one command instead of a five-step checklist, and a session that stops early leaves an item that is *visibly* unconverged rather than one that looks done and isn't.

Worth doing before the fleet flip's per-member burst multiplies the number of sessions performing this by hand.

---
Triage **one** open issue and take the **first** applicable action. This **acts** — but every action defaults to the reversible option when the check is inconclusive.

- **Already implemented in `main`** → **close** (`completed`) + a one-line comment citing where it landed.
- **Conflicts with a current guideline** → label `needs-decision` + a comment naming the conflict.
- **Blocked by another issue** → label `blocked` + a comment `blocked by #N`.
- **Small and quick to do** → label `quick-win` + a comment scoping it.
- **Else** → leave it.

**"Implemented in `main`" means the issue's actual ask is true of `main`'s content _now_** — confirm it there and cite it (file/line or specific content). **Never** infer it from a linked PR merging or the issue merely looking done. If you can't point to it, **comment, don't close.** Create the label if it's missing (labels almost certainly already exist in this repo from prior runs of this same skill — check with mcp__github__get_label first, and if genuinely absent, add the label anyway via the issue-write labels update, GitHub will reject silently-created labels are not auto-created by REST so just try adding it and if it errors, note that in your result and skip the label but still post the comment). Return `{ action, note }` (action one of closed/needs-decision/blocked/quick-win/left/unchanged).

## Never re-post a verdict you already posted

A triage comment updates the issue, and an updated issue is the next window's touched-issue trigger — so a comment that only restates the last one wakes this task again tomorrow, and again the day after. The verdict is the news; re-deriving it is not.

Before writing anything, read the issue's comments and find the most recent one this task posted — by its marker (`<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=... -->`), or, on an issue triaged before the marker existed, by its wording. If the action you are about to take is the one that comment already announced, **post nothing and change nothing** (a label already on the issue included) and return `{ action: 'unchanged', note: '<action> since <its date>' }`. Closing is never a repeat: it changes the issue's state and ends the sequence.

End every comment you post with this marker, alone on the last line:
```
<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=<action> -->
```
---

Important context for judging "implemented in main": the local git checkout at /home/user/Claudinite has its HEAD (commit 65f1d62) IDENTICAL to origin/main right now, so you can and should use Read/Grep/Glob/Bash directly against this working directory as your source of truth for "main's current content" — it's faster and more reliable than fetching file contents via the GitHub API. Cite specific file paths/line numbers or content when you close an issue as implemented.

"Conflicts with a current guideline" means the issue's ask contradicts something now stated as settled policy in CLAUDE.md / packs/*/RULES.md / skills — read the relevant pack's RULES.md if the issue's topic maps to one.

When done with all 8 issues, report back a compact list: for each issue number, the action taken (closed/needs-decision/blocked/quick-win/left/unchanged) and a one-line note. This is critical — I need this list to reconcile a tracking issue, so be precise and complete, don't summarize away any issue.

- adopt-claudinite: Bootstrap Claudinite into a consuming repo — mount, hooks, checks, skills. Use when asked to bootstrap, adopt, or set up Claudinite, or to baseline a repo to pick up updates.
- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- bump-version: Raise the project's version — a minor bump by default. Use when the owner says "bump version".
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and extract its working instructions into reusable canon packs plus the project's own local packs (.claudinite/local_packs/). Use when a project has no established working style yet, or it exhibits a facet no pack covers — during bootstrap of a fresh/empty repo, or on an uplevel request.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- single-branch-status: Assess one branch's landed status — merged, already-in-main, superseded, orphaned, or genuine unmerged work — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single branch is safe to delete, judging by content not the ref's name (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-branches task hands you branches to assess).
- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. Use when acting on a single issue; "implemented in main" must be verified against main's current content and the default is to comment, not close (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-issues task hands you issues to triage).
- single-pr-status: Assess one open pull request's landed status — keep-open, or closeable (merged, already-in-main, superseded, stale) — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single PR should stay open, judging by its commits and diff not its title (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-prs task hands you PRs to assess).
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- writing-claudinite-skills: Authoring or changing a skill in the Claudinite corpus — SKILL.md conventions, where a skill's checks and tests live, catalog and pack wiring. Use when creating or editing a pack's skills/<name>/ in the canon; a consumer project's own agent docs are authoring-agent-docs' turf.
- writing-migration-plans: How to order the phases of an implementation or migration plan so nothing stalls mid-run — front-load the out-of-band setup, collapse the review gates into one stacked-PR pass, leave only executable steps — and how to keep its tracking issue append-only while implementing. Use when writing or reviewing a migration plan or a phased implementation plan, and when working through one's tracking issue.
- writing-tasks: The contract a Claudinite task is written to — the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the precondition as the only decision point, ordering, and how a work item converges. Use when writing or changing a tasks/<name>/task.mjs or its worker, or when a task-declaration check fires.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.
- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. {"number":942,"title":"Dashboard sign-in: register the GitHub App and deploy the code-exchange endpoint","body":"The dashboard's sign-in path is built and tested ([#935](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/935)), but it stays dormant until two things exist that only an account owner can create. Until then every deployment falls back to the token-paste box.

## Why these can't be automated

A static page cannot reuse a visitor's github.com login: session cookies are not sent to `api.github.com`, and the API refuses cookie auth cross-origin. So "no typing" has to mean an OAuth sign-in. The `code` → token exchange needs the app's **client secret** and targets an endpoint that sends **no CORS headers**, so it cannot happen in the browser — it needs one small hosted function.

## Steps

- [ ] **Register a GitHub App** (or OAuth App) on the `missingbulb` account.
  - Callback URL: the deployed dashboard's URL, exactly — e.g. `https://missingbulb.github.io/Sheepdog/`.
  - Request **read-only** Contents, Issues, Metadata and Actions.
  - Note the **Client ID**; generate a **Client secret**.
  - *While absent:* no Sign in button renders anywhere; the token box is the only way in.

- [ ] **Deploy the exchange endpoint.** Paste [`oauth-exchange.example.mjs`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/claudinite-tasks-dashboard-20xby9/engine/scheduler/dashboard/oauth-exchange.example.mjs) into a Cloudflare Worker (or Netlify/Vercel function — same handler, different wrapper). Set `GITHUB_CLIENT_ID`, `GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET`, and `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` to the exact page origin.
  - *While absent:* clicking Sign in would return to a page that cannot complete the exchange, so the button stays hidden — the config gates on both halves together.
  - It sees one code and returns one token. It never proxies repo data and stores nothing.

- [ ] **Install the App** on the account/org so it can see the member repos.
  - *While absent:* sign-in succeeds but repos read as 404 — the token carries no installation.

- [ ] **Write `dashboard.config.json`** beside the deployed page with `clientId` and `exchangeUrl` (see [`dashboard.config.example.json`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/claudinite-tasks-dashboard-20xby9/engine/scheduler/dashboard/dashboard.config.example.json)). It is written by the deploying site, never committed into the vendored tree.
  - *While absent:* token fallback.

## Closing condition

Loading the deployed dashboard signed out shows **Sign in with GitHub**; clicking it returns you signed in, with your avatar in the header and a repo you can read rendering — and no token ever typed.

{"number":926,"title":"The declarative vocabulary has never reached a member's local pack — fleet census, and the one key that is missing","body":"#880 closed the coded→declared question for the **canon**. This is the same question asked of the **fleet**, and the answer is different: the canon is 49/85 declared, and until today every member repo was **0**.

## Census (2026-08-16, each member's `main`, shallow clones)

Local-pack rule modules, excluding `pack.mjs` / `lib.mjs` / task workers / tests:

| repo | local packs | coded rules | declarations |
|---|---|---|---|
| CrosswordChat | 2 | 8 | 0 |
| EdFringeNow | 3 | 7 | 0 |
| VascularColoring | 1 | 7 | 0 |
| GoogleCalendarEventCreator | 1 | 5 | 0 |
| Sheepdog | 1 | 5 | 0 |
| gRatio | 1 | 5 | 0 |
| HelloWorldFlutterApp | 1 | 5 | 0 |
| LaughCounter | 3 | 10 → **5** | **2 files, 5 rules** |
| ClaudiniteCanary | 1 | 4 | 0 |
| ShoutsAndWhispers | 1 | 4 | 0 |
| TLDR | 1 | 2 | 0 |
| **total** | **16** | **62 → 57** | **5** |

LaughCounter's column moved today — missingbulb/LaughCounter#203 converts five, the first declarations in any member repo.

## Two members cannot carry a declaration at all

`HelloWorldFlutterApp` and `gRatio` have no `engine/checks/helpers/pattern-rules.mjs` in their mount, so their 10 rules are not a conversion backlog — they are a **convergence** finding. Both last moved 2026-08-12. Worth reading their stamps and the head sha's runs before anything else is proposed for them, per the standing "read the member's own artifacts first" rule.

## The one missing vocabulary key, with two named customers

Every content assertion in the vocabulary predicates on a file's **text**. Two fleet rules assert about a **path's existence alone**:

- `vascular-coloring/rendered-overlays-untracked` — no tracked image under `analysis/`
- `edfringe/no-stray-package-json` — no `package.json` outside the root and a grandfathered `plan/`

`repoWide.flagFilesMatching` matches text, so today these convert only by pairing a path-selecting `scanFiles` with an always-true content regex — a hack that reads as nothing. The honest form is a `forbidPathsMatching` assertion (pattern + exceptions + `what`/`fix`), which is the exact negative of the existing `requirePaths`. Both customers exist now; I'd build it against them rather than speculatively.

## What the rest of the fleet's rules actually are

All 62 were signal-classified (transcript / git / parse / derived-scan-set / config), and ~15 read in full — so treat the per-rule verdicts below as firm and the residue as classified but not individually argued to #880's standard.

The residue falls into the same classes #880 named, and the fleet is if anything *more* weighted to them, because a local pack exists precisely to carry what the canon shelf could not:

- **Derived scan set / derived key set** — the largest group. `shouts-and-whispers/cross-tier-constant-coverage` quantifies over constants discovered in one tier and looks for them in another *and* in the guard's own `PAIRS` map; `canary/pack-shape` reads the skill names out of `pack.mjs` and checks each named file exists.
- **Needs a real parser** — `edfringe-data/normalizer-selftest-in-verify` strips `step "…"` labels out of a shell script before looking for the command, precisely because a grep for the two tokens is satisfied by the label alone.
- **Computation** — `vascular-coloring/overlay-color-contrast` parses `(r, g, b)` literals and asserts `r - g >= 60 && r - b >= 60`. No pattern language expresses that, and it should not try.
- **Imports the definition it guards** — several read a constant or list out of the very code they check, which is the class where coded is the *stronger* rung.

Two near-misses worth naming, both one key from convertible:

- `on-device-privacy/on-device-speech` (LaughCounter) — asserts an opt-out appears within **12 lines after** a construction. `andIndentedBlockBelowMatches` does not fit: the opt-out sits at the same indentation, not inside a block. A "within the next N lines" relation would convert it.
- `macos-audio/swift-toolchain-gate`, `signal-teardown-routing` — both assert **ordering** (a probe sits behind a gate; `SIG_IGN` precedes `resume()`), which the vocabulary has no relation for.

## Suggested order

1. Diagnose the two stale mounts — a member that cannot compile a declaration is the blocking item, and it is not about checks at all.
2. `forbidPathsMatching`, red-first against its two customers, then convert them in their repos.
3. Judge the "within the next N lines" relation on its own merits, with `on-device-speech` as the single customer — one customer may not earn a key, and #880's `matchAnyValueOfSet` is the precedent for declining.

Nothing here proposes converting the residue. The point of the census is the opposite: to have the number, and the reason for each rule that keeps its module.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/926","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-16T11:48:13Z","updated_at":"2026-08-16T11:48:13Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":170,"title":"Revisit: Workflow tool's interactive opt-in blocks unattended routines (waiting on Anthropic)","body":"## The limitation

The multi-agent-orchestration **`Workflow`** tool requires an **interactive human opt-in on every run** ("Allow Claude to run a workflow?"). That prompt only disappears under bypass-permissions / headless modes a scheduler can't be relied on to be in. Because an unattended routine has no human to click **Allow**, any routine that fans out through the Workflow tool stalls on step one.

This also means the tool's nicest ergonomics are off-limits to us for unattended work: committing a Workflow script and having the nightly job just run it by name (`Workflow({name: ...})`) hits the **same** prompt — the gate is on *invoking* a workflow, not on authoring one. And the parallel-agent step can't be pushed into a plain committed script either, since spawning Claude subagents is a harness capability, not something arbitrary code can call.

## Our current workaround

We fan the fleet daily maintenance routine out with **plain subagent dispatch** (the Agent/Task tool) instead, which carries no opt-in gate, and the orchestrator honors the phase barriers itself. See #168 / #169 and `routines/auto-all-repos-maintenance.md` + `skills/unattended-agents/SKILL.md`.

This works and is the right default (no dependency on an out-of-repo permission-mode setting), but it costs us the Workflow tool's built-in phase/barrier machinery and the option to run committed, reviewed orchestration code.

## Why keep this open

This is a limitation of the platform, not our code — we're **waiting on the world to change**. If Anthropic later lets an unattended session pre-authorize the Workflow tool (a settings allowlist entry, an environment/routine permission mode that reliably suppresses just this prompt, or persisted per-workflow consent that survives a fresh cloud clone), we could reconsider using committed Workflow scripts for the fleet routine and get determinism + review back.

**Action:** periodically check with Anthropic / the Claude Code release notes whether the Workflow tool can be pre-authorized for unattended sessions. When it can, revisit the plain-dispatch decision in the routine spec.

{"number":803,"title":"Every dispatch starts two executor sessions; one burns a container to stand down","body":"**Corrected.** I filed this claiming the claim protocol is not exclusive. That was wrong, and the correction matters because the original framing would have sent someone to fix something that already works.

`engine/scheduler/executor.md` step 2 already specifies read → swap → **re-read**, with earliest-claim-wins and an explicit "end the session without dispatching" for the loser. On the observed run the protocol did exactly that: two claims, one delivery commit, PR merged once. What I saw was the guard working.

## The real issue: the duplicate firing itself

Two sessions still start for one dispatch. `ClaudiniteCanary#62`:

```
Claimed by executor session (Claude Code, session f29055ea-…) at 2026-08-13T19:24:34Z.
Claimed by executor session `91596dae-…`               at 2026-08-13T19:24:38Z.
```

`fileHandoff` creates the issue with **both** labels in a single POST (`labels: [readyLabel, escalation.name]`), so this is not two label-add calls from our side. GitHub emits a `labeled` event per label on creation, so a routine triggering on `labeled` fires twice.

That costs a whole container and model session per dispatch to do nothing but read labels and quit, on **every** escalated dispatch across the fleet. It also leaves a stray claim comment on every such issue, which is what made me misread the protocol in the first place — the artifact of a correctly-handled race is indistinguishable at a glance from a race that wasn't handled.

## Worth fixing, in order of cheapness

1. **File the issue with the ready label only**, and add the escalation label in a follow-up call *after* creation. One `labeled` event at create → one firing. The escalation label stays countable. (Check that the follow-up add doesn't itself re-fire the routine — if it does, this doesn't help and the fix is 2 or 3.)
2. **Have the routine trigger on `opened` rather than `labeled`**, filtered by label. Lives in the CCR routine config, outside this repo.
3. **Have the losing session delete its own claim comment** before standing down, so a handled race leaves no trace. Cosmetic, but it removes the misreading this issue is evidence of.

## Also observed

The two claim comments use different wording — one names "(Claude Code, session …)", the other backticks the id alone. That suggests the two sessions were running different vendored generations of `executor.md`, which is worth understanding independently: the routine's two firings may not be picking up the same instructions.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/803","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["quick-win"],"comments":3,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-13T19:32:27Z","updated_at":"2026-08-15T04:21:36Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

[{"id":5287965358,"body":"Comment class: other

Investigated. Three findings, one of which corrects the issue.

**"Also observed" is wrong — the two sessions ran the same instructions.** `executor.md` step 2.2 says only "post a claim comment naming this session and the UTC time"; it gives no template, so the wording is free-form model prose and two sessions on identical instructions will naturally differ. Independently: the fleet routine's sources do not include ClaudiniteCanary, and there is exactly one `Claudinite executor - ClaudiniteCanary` routine. Both sessions came from that one routine. There is no vendored-generation skew to understand.

**Option 3 is not implementable as written.** The executor session is MCP-only, and the GitHub MCP server exposes no delete-comment or edit-comment tool — `add_issue_comment` is the whole surface. The loser cannot withdraw its claim. #811 does the reachable version: it states the stand-down on the issue, so the artifact reads unambiguously as a handled race, and unlike deletion it leaves the duplicate countable while the duplicate is still unfixed.

**Option 1 looks ineffective, and the reason is the observation itself.** If the routine matched on the *added* label name, a create with two labels would match once and one session would start. Two started. So the routine is firing on something broader — the issue carrying the ready label whatever the event, or `opened` and `labeled` both. Under either, adding the escalation label in a follow-up call still fires it a second time, and the extra POST buys nothing.

I can't settle which, because the firing rule lives in the CCR routine config and `list_triggers` returns the launcher prompt, model and sources but no event or label filter. What settles it: file a dispatch-shaped issue with the ready label only and count the sessions. One → the trigger is `labeled`-with-a-broad-filter and option 1 is worth doing; two → it also fires on `opened` and only option 2 (trigger on `opened`, filtered by label) fixes it. That's a live firing of a real executor, so it's yours to run rather than mine.

One option the list doesn't have, cheapest of all if you'll take the trade: **drop the escalation label and count the code off the dispatch body**, which already carries it (`run.mjs` passes `reason` into `dispatchBody`). One label at creation is one event under every hypothesis above. The cost is that the condition stops being countable by label search, which is the reason you added it — your call, not mine.

Worth noting on urgency: this costs one wasted container per *escalated* dispatch, not per dispatch — an unescalated one is filed with a single label. The loser exits at step 2.3 without writing, so the waste is bounded and nothing runs twice. And `docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` replaces this trigger path wholesale; option 2's config change may be work you do once and then discard.
