{"number":801,"title":"Migration to the work-item queue: two PRs, one same-day validation burst","body":"The phase plan for [tasks-dispatch DESIGN](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md) (§14 points here). Design constraints from the owner (2026-08-13): **fewest disparate steps, fewest approval points, and certainty the same day** — we do not wait for a nightly run to learn whether the end state works. Deliberately generating real work to push traffic through every path is explicitly sanctioned.

**Approval points: two.** PR‑1 (mechanism + canon flip) and PR‑2 (fleet flip + slot deletion). Everything else is forcing and observing, which the mechanism itself defines as ordinary operations.

Checkboxes track progress; each burst row's checkbox is checked only with an evidence URL appended beside it.

---

## Where this stands (2026-08-16 12:10Z)

**One member is verified end to end, agentic lane included. Twelve more are blocked on owner-only credential work.** Steps 0–2 complete. Step 3 is most of the way: the flip is merged and observed, the first member ran a real agentic item to `outcome:done`, and three defects the burst could not have caught were found and two fixed. The slot deletion still waits on the remaining members.

| | state |
|---|---|
| Canon | on the queue since #854; 12 clean scheduler runs overnight, 12 items to terminal state |
| Fleet | flipped by default in #888 (`17902b9`); **GCEC verified end to end**, 12 members still need a CCR routine (#916) |
| Slot machinery | still in the tree, deliberately — deleting it before members are verified strands them (see Step 3) |
| Design vs engine | DESIGN/sim current to §15.24 plus F24; engine at pre-review behavior — the catch-up is Step 4 (#883) |
| Open follow-ups | #916 (owner-only, blocking), #921, #892, #924, #883, #877 |

## Step 0 — rehearsal (done)

- [x] Simulator + scenario suite green in CI; coverage map names the live-only rows

## Step 1 — PR‑1 on canon: the whole mechanism, canon flipped (approval №1)

- [x] Label vocabulary, tick workflow (cron + `workflow_dispatch`), executor workflow, janitor re-target, dependency fields + `after` yield + `create-work-item`, F8 signal exclusions, canon flipped, gate green
- [x] **Approval №1: PR‑1 merged** — #854, `b30ef77`

## Step 2 — the validation burst (complete)

- [x] **B1 creation + first-item rule (S25):** [run 31899008771](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31899008771) — 12 items #860–#870, each `task:blocked` wearing its next anchor
- [x] **B2 the roll + reasons on record (S1′):** #860 — one ask, rolled to tomorrow, reason on the item, no comment spam
- [x] **B3 agentic happy path + real CCR invocation + records (S2):** #867 — wake → claim → hand-off with nonce → **live session in 31s** → result + exec record → `outcome:done`
- [x] **B4 agentless path end to end:** #859 — wake → executor in 2s → claim → prework → `outcome:done`, closed in 26s, no session
- [x] **B5 the chain + yield (S4/S23):** #863 — yielded while `core/update` was live ([run 31913047785](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31913047785)), then claimed and running the moment the upstream cleared; its work merged as #887
- [x] ~~**B6 hourly cadence**~~ — **dropped** (owner). `create-extractor` is `gcec/create-extractor` on GoogleCalendarEventCreator, the fleet's only hourly task; canon has none
- [x] ~~**B7 missing-secret posture**~~ — **folded into Step 3** (owner): every member reaches the flip with its endpoint token unset, so the posture happens on real traffic with no scaffolding
- [x] **B8 force-while-executing mutex (S15):** #871 — queued behind the executing twin, then got its own verdict on release
- [x] **B9 multi-executor lease (S7):** #873 — three overlapping executors, exactly one claim, one execution
- [x] **B10 follow-up fields (S17):** #872 — `Blocked-by` + `Not-before` created and held blocked by the tick
- [x] **B11 janitor leashes:** [run 31900490000](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31900490000) — 12 blocked/rolling items, zero escalations
- [x] **All burst rows green**

### What the burst caught that the rehearsal could not

Four defects, none of which any simulator would have produced. Three are fixed:

- **#879 → #881 (merged).** Hand-off appended a second `### Context` instead of replacing the first, splitting the item's binding scope while `instructions.md` says to read "the Context section", singular. Every unit test passed, because each tested one call. Confirmed fixed on live traffic in B5's own hand-off.
- **#882 → #885 (merged).** Queue sessions wrote `[unknown]` where the exec record's slot id used to go — `instructions.md` never said what replaces it — dropping the join from a record back to its work item.
- **The task-path guard fired correctly** on a hand-built item naming `task.mjs` instead of `task.md` (#871): refused, converged to `needs-human`, nothing run.
- **#892 (open).** The terminal convergence is agent-discretion, and **both** agentic runs got part of it wrong — #867's record field, and #863 closing with no outcome label and no exec record at all. Proposes a `converge-item.mjs` the session calls with its judged outcome.

## Step 3 — the fleet flip, then the deletion (approval №2)

**PR‑2 is two PRs, not one** (amendment, 2026-08-15). The plan said "slot machinery deleted in this same PR"; that is unsafe, and the reason is in the code:

- `updates/engine-update.mjs` **replaces the mount wholesale**, so a file canon deletes leaves every member's mount on its next converge whatever that member's config says.
- `.github/workflows/` is the one path a converge cannot push — staged, and landed later by the apply stage.
- The two stubs call **different entry points**: `run.mjs` vs `queue/tick.mjs`.

So deleting slots in the flip's own release strands any member whose workflow has not yet landed. Keeping the slot code makes that window benign (`run.mjs` no-ops) and #888 makes it **loud**.

- [x] The pack update flow staged only the scheduler workflow, so `claudinite-executor.yml` reached no member — #874, `5ca4c35`
- [x] **Approval №2: the flip merged** — #888, `17902b9`. `dispatchMode` answers `queue` for an absent setting, so members flip with **no edit to any file they own**
- [x] **A member's converge observed** — GoogleCalendarEventCreator, 2026-08-16 02:00:18–02:00:25Z: both stubs call the queue entry points out of the mount, `taskScheduler` carries no `dispatch` key, mount `queue/tick.mjs` byte-identical to canon HEAD, and [15 standing items created](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/918) (GCEC #904–#918). Last slot-era item was GCEC #903 at 00:09Z
- [x] **B7 lands here** — and the fault was **not** the unset secret the plan anticipated. `resolveEndpoint` fails at the *declaration*: [GCEC #908](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/908#issuecomment-5305803329) parked `needs-human` naming `taskScheduler.endpoints`, no session started. `endpoints` was declared in exactly one repo in the fleet — this one — so the flip left **every** member's agentic lane dark
- [x] **Per-member mini-burst on the first member (B1–B4 + B7 + B3 agentic)** — GCEC: agentless lane ran clean from 02:00Z; [GCEC #908 closed `outcome:done` at 11:28:16Z](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/908) via a live session started 11:16:12Z, its work landing as GCEC #923; [GCEC #907 `core/update`](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/907) closed `outcome:done` 11:49:02Z, converging the mount through the queue itself
- [ ] **The other 12 members wired and observed** — blocked on #916 (owner-only: one CCR routine + `CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN` per repo)
- [ ] #921 folded in — DESIGN §8's force recipe yields an item `pickOrder` can never pick
- [ ] **Then** the slot deletion PR (slots.mjs, run-ledger math, exclusive claim, re-arm, `FORCE_TASKS` path, slot-conformance checks)
- [ ] The migration reports itself through the mechanism it ships: per-member fan-out items + a fan-in item `Blocked-by` all of them (S18 live) — fan-in closed `outcome:done`

### What Step 3 caught that Step 2 could not

Three defects, each invisible to the burst for a specific reason — and the reasons are the finding:

- **#906 → #907 (merged).** `queue/instructions.md` was never in the vendor set: `computeVendorSet` drops every `engine/**/*.md` behind a two-entry operational whitelist, and #854 added a third operational doc without extending it. That file *is* the behavior of a work-item session. **Invisible because canon runs the engine from its repo root, not a mount** — so no amount of canon traffic could show it.
- **#922 → #925 (merged).** F18's episode boundary was stated semantically and implemented over only the paths that already wrote a comment; the roll and the `needs-human` park end an episode silently, leaving a claim that outranks every future claimant. The roll self-heals via the leash (canon #860 sat unrunnable 17:44Z→03:32Z); the park never does. Fixed by *striking* the claim — including on the **losing** claimant, whose claim would otherwise become the earliest of the next episode. **Invisible because the simulator modelled the rule's intent rather than its artifact**, so it was correct by construction; the sim now models the artifact and reproduces the bug without the fix.
- **#921 (open).** DESIGN §8's force recipe — strip `task:blocked`, optionally add `task:urgent` — omits `task:ready`, and `pickOrder` admits on `task:ready` alone. A forced item is invisible to every executor and the run logs `nothing ready to pick up`, which looks exactly like a healthy run. **Invisible because no executable artifact pins DESIGN's prose recipes.**

## Step 4 — the work-as-work engine catch-up (#883; starts only after Step 3's verification)

#884 (merged 2026-08-16, `4380639`) changed the design under the shipped mechanism — decisions §15.14–24. **The behavior-by-behavior checklist lives in #883** — one box per capability, each stating what breaks while it's off; this plan owns only the sequencing:

- [ ] **Step 4 waits for Step 3's per-member verification** — the flip wave must be observed on the engine it shipped, not one changing underneath it
- [ ] Each #883 behavior lands burst-style per this plan's own discipline: a forced run observed on canon the same day; the workflow-touching pieces (heartbeat, decoupling, continuation job, suspend-all) additionally observed on one member's converge before the fleet's
- [ ] #892's `converge-item.mjs` is the natural carrier for #883's durable-record box — land them together, not twice
- [ ] #924 (a losing claimant's comment defers the leash reclaim) rides #883's heartbeat, which introduces the per-holder liveness signal it needs
- [ ] #877 (the tick rename) unblocks when this step closes — last, so the rename never churns files mid-migration

## Done means

- [x] All Step‑2 rows have evidence URLs on this issue
- [x] The first member flipped, wired and observed end to end — agentless and agentic
- [ ] All members flipped and observed; fan-in item closed `outcome:done`
- [ ] Slot machinery gone from the tree
- [ ] Step 4: the fielded engine matches DESIGN §15.14–24 — #883 closed
- [ ] 48h of ordinary operation as *confirmation* — explicitly not the proof; the burst was the proof

{"number":841,"title":"pack.json migration plan: engine reader + canon conversion, then a versioned fleet migration","body":"Executes #564 (re-evaluated 2026-08-14; PR #569 reviewed for insights and closed). Owner-settled decisions this plan encodes:

- **`pack.schema.json` is authoring tooling** (editor autocomplete + documentation). Manifest conformance — field shapes, the 20-word routing cap, skills↔tree, rule-scope agreement, the accounted-for-`.mjs` guard — is **checked by the world sweep when the file is edited**, not at load. The loader stays minimal and fail-soft: parse, resolve filenames, surface unreadable/unparseable as blocking config findings (as today).
- **`detect` is data for 14 of 17 packs** (path matching + content matching, full-noun-phrase keys per the #789/#799 discipline); sibling `detect.mjs` for chrome-extension, chrome-extension-release, static-website.
- **Members' local packs convert via a `basics` migration record with `applyStage`**; the routing gap that makes `basics` the carrier for an engine-owned format is #840.

Owner approval points: **two PRs** (plus one small telemetry-gated retirement PR later). Everything else lands through the members' own auto-merged update PRs.

## PR 1 — the engine reads pack.json; the whole canon converts

One PR: the reader and the corpus it reads must land transactionally, and the home (no mount, runs repo-root code) is the first consumer either way.

- [ ] `engine/pack_loader/pack.schema.json` — the authoring spec; its field order is the one canonical order (no second list).
- [ ] Registry reads `pack.json`: prefers it where `pack.mjs` coexists (a half-finished conversion must not resolve to the old shape), reports the leftover module for deletion, stamps `manifestFile` so findings name the consumer's actual file. The `pack.mjs` import path stays as the tolerance branch.
- [ ] `detect` spec compiler (tracked-path + file-content matching), with the #569-style equivalence tests: each compiled spec proven to mean exactly what the arrow it replaces meant — including the near-root `maxDepth` semantics and the jwt/web-speech/leaflet content-regex shape.
- [ ] Sibling code files named from the JSON: `detect.mjs` ×3, `env.mjs` where env is a function of config (node; flutter's static shell as data if the spec carries a line list, else a second `env.mjs`), `contributed.mjs` ×2 (barriers, canary-probe); `contributes` becomes a map of pack id → rule filenames; `worldRules`/`workRules` become filename lists (manifest placement stays the scope authority — #555; `declared-checks.json` stays structural with no manifest line — #827).
- [ ] Manifest conformance moves to the world sweep: schema shape, routing word cap, skills↔tree, scope agreement, and the every-`.mjs`-at-pack-root-accounted-for guard. Author each check first and watch it fail (a deliberately broken fixture AND a live in-scope count over the real tree — a path-pattern check that reaches zero files passes silently).
- [ ] Convert all 33 canon manifests + the home's 2 local packs; genuinely unhoused comments move to each pack's README (#569's second commit has the survey).
- [ ] Repoint every `pack.mjs` reader, enumerated from `grep -rl 'pack\.mjs'` in-branch (today: `vendoring/compute-vendor-set.mjs`, sheepdog `fleet-pack-seeds`, `adopt-claudinite` interview, `converge-wiring`, the seededByDefault audit, the pack-prose narration rule, ~20 test fixtures). Fixtures author `pack.json` and copy `engine/pack_loader/` wholesale rather than enumerating its modules.
- [ ] Full suite via `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`; conformance sweep green; both hand-maintained tallies recomputed (not incremented) if checks were added; suite re-run against current `main` immediately before merge.

**Verified in-session**: the home *is* the corpus, so a green selftest + world sweep on the converted tree is a real end-to-end run of the reader — plus one member repo attached read-only to confirm nothing in its (unconverted) mount breaks against canon-side tasks that read packs from a fresh clone.

## Between PRs — the release gate

- [ ] Run the live canary rehearsal against the merged snapshot; watch it to a terminal state (a dispatch is not a result). Note its known blind spot: it drives the worker *this ref ships*, so it cannot see a fielded-caller break — hence the next checkbox.
- [ ] Confirm nothing under `updates/*` (the flow surface fielded workers call) changed shape in PR 1; if anything did, shim per the live-cross-version-API discipline before releasing.

## PR 2 — the release and the fleet migration record, one change

Per `engine/migrations/README.md`, a record lands in the same change as the bump it names:

- [ ] `ENGINE_VERSION` 4 → 5 (the engine that reads pack.json).
- [ ] `basics` version 2 → 3, `minEngineVersion: 5` — the updater's own enforcement guarantees no member converts its local packs before holding the engine that reads the result.
- [ ] `packs/basics/migrations/2026-08-XX-local-pack-json/migration.mjs`:
  - `applyStage: { why, instructions }` — convert this repo's local packs to `pack.json` (+ sibling `.mjs` only where a manifest genuinely holds code), move manifest comments to the pack README, delete `pack.mjs`, repair the member's own pack tests.
  - `legacyPresent` probes every declared local pack (both local-pack roots) for a surviving `pack.mjs` — the fleet census reads it, so "is the fleet done" is telemetry, not memory.
  - `appliesTo` probes the member's own mount for the pack.json-capable registry **by content, not version stamp** — fail-safe (unreadable mount = not capable), so the record delays instead of wedging (the sheepdog-fleet-baseline lesson).

## Same-session fleet verification — not "after the nightly"

- [ ] Force the fleet baseline/update sweep with `follow`; report per-member results unasked, attaching member repos directly rather than offering to.
- [ ] Drive one member that carries local packs through its update **now**; watch the `applyStage` session convert them and the auto-merged PR land green.
- [ ] Judge freshness by each member's stamp `ref`/engine version, never `updated` alone (held stamps), and read the **status** of every API write, not just its body.
- [ ] Report the `legacyPresent` census: which members still hold a `pack.mjs`, driven by the standing update mechanism — no phase anyone must remember to close.

## Retirement — telemetry-gated, expiry-pinned

- [ ] PR 1 ships a pinned-expiry test on the both-shapes tolerance (re-check at a named engine version), so retirement has a trigger that comes to us.
- [ ] When the census reads clean **from the members' repos, not by reasoning about canon**: one small PR deletes the `pack.mjs` read branch and the legacy fixtures. The record itself stays, as history.

Status note from the #649 verification run; nothing here is decided or changed.

One risk this issue carries implicitly is now retired. The acceptance probe — "purge all release aspects from MissingBulbWebsite so it simulates a fresh repo, adopt the pack, and the first release works on the first go" — depends on `static-website`'s `static-site-vendoring` record materializing four workflows into the repo's own `.github/workflows/`. The pack has zero adopters, so that record had never delivered anything to anyone.

Nor had **any** record: a `materialize` whose `dest` is under `.github/workflows/` had never run against a live member, which is the residual #649 was reopened for. It is not a benign untested path — the update flow commits with the Action's `GITHUB_TOKEN`, GitHub refuses it there, and the refusal rejects the *whole ref*. A broken lane would have failed the first adopter's entire converge, and the acceptance probe would have been the thing that discovered it.

Verified end to end on the canary on 2026-08-14 (evidence on #649), through the same `write` `static-site-vendoring` uses: withheld to `.claudinite/pending-workflows/`, carried in the PR, parked at `apply-stage`, moved into `.github/workflows/` byte-for-byte by a session, staging swept.

So the vendoring half of the adoption path is no longer an unknown going into this work. One caveat found in the same run and worth knowing before the probe is timed: the apply stage did not merge its own PR, so delivery waited for the next cycle's disposal — on a daily `update`, up to 24h. Fix in #832; without it, "the first release works on the first go" could look like a failure that is really a wait.

The design's open questions, lifted out of `DESIGN.md` so they are decidable here rather than inside a merged doc. Nothing is decided or changed by this comment.

The design landed in #723. Three questions it deliberately left to the owner:

### 1. Pack name — `static-website` or `github-pages-serving`?

Cosmetic. The task framing called for a "github-pages-serving pack", but the pack owns versioning and the CI gate as well as the Pages deploy, so the broader name is arguably the more accurate one. **Default if unanswered: keep `static-website`** — renaming costs a vendored-path migration across adopters and buys nothing the id doesn't already say.

### 2. EdFringeNow data refreshes — `deploy-only`, or full releases?

This is the one with a live consequence, and **as adopted neither behaviour is happening**. EdFringeNow's #319 states the expectation that hourly refreshes keep cutting releases ("roughly 17/day"). They don't: the refresh task runs inside the scheduler workflow and pushes with its `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which fires no `push` event, so the release orchestrator never starts.

Confirmed against the repo since adoption:

- `bb3089c` (2026-08-12 05:22Z, "Refresh Fringe data (daily top-up)" — a scheduler-authored push into the publish set) cut **no release**. The data went live 7.5 hours later, carried incidentally by `v1.60812.1`, which was triggered by a human PR merge.
- Four releases in the five days since adoption, against five version bumps on the single day before it.
- Nothing has landed in `data/` since that release, so the live site is not stale *right now* — the gap has bitten once, visibly, rather than continuously. The daily-instead-of-hourly change (EdFringeNow #340) narrows the exposure but does not touch the cause.

So the question is not "which cadence do we prefer" but "what should a data push do", and either answer needs wiring that doesn't exist yet:

- **`deploy-only`** (the design's D5/D6 recommendation): the refresh task dispatches the release workflow in a mode that assembles and deploys the current tip without bumping, tagging, or cutting a Release. Fresh data reaches the site; tags keep naming content releases.
- **Full releases per data push**: same dispatch wiring, no new mode — accept a tag + GitHub Release per refresh (~1/day at the current cadence, ~17/day if hourly returns next festival).

Doing nothing keeps today's behaviour, where data reaches the site only when unrelated content ships.

### 3. The public beacon token — commit it, or keep `build_vars`?

The design's D3 argues each site should commit its Cloudflare Web Analytics token directly and delete the injection machinery: the token ships to every visitor in the page, so the repo variable protects nothing, and what it buys (rotation without a commit; forks not inheriting live analytics) is thin against a config key, an exporter, a drift guard, a placeholder convention and a per-repo injection script.

The fleet has since answered the other way in practice — #729's `build_vars` is merged and live on EdFringeNow. It is a well-built mechanism and strictly better than the wholesale export it replaced (#626, closed): a declared list keeps repo vocabulary out of the copy-verbatim stubs, fail-on-unset stops a deleted variable from silently shipping a beaconless site, and being handed only the `vars` context means a secret structurally cannot reach the build.

The design still recommends D3, on the grounds that `build_vars` can carry *only* non-secret values by construction — and any value safe to put in a repo variable is safe to commit — so every possible use of the key has a simpler equivalent in source. **If D3 is accepted, a follow-on question:** retire the `build_vars` capability from the pack once its only user is gone, or keep it dormant for a future build-time value that genuinely varies per environment?

1	# Making changes to Claudinite without hurting consumers
2	
3	> **Status: provisional — beliefs, not law.** Every entry here says what we're *currently* doing
4	> and *why we think* it helps. When an entry blocks a better change, challenge the entry rather
5	> than contorting the change; being cited in this guide is not, by itself, a reason something
6	> must stay. We'll solidify entries once they've earned it.
7	
8	Claudinite is vendored into every consuming repo, so a change here lands in many places, on the
9	fleet's schedule, usually with no human watching. This guide collects what we currently believe
10	about making such changes safely. It is a maintainer document for sessions working *in* this
11	repo; it is not part of the vendored corpus.
12	
13	## First, know which channel the change travels
14	
15	Since the fleet moved to the tracked vendored mount (vendoring/DESIGN.md, phases 1–3 complete),
16	the channel model is small — nothing reaches a consumer instantly, and nothing arrives outside
17	its git history:
18	
19	- **The vendored corpus** (`engine/`, `packs/` — checks, prose, bundled skills) — each member
20	  holds a tracked snapshot under `.claudinite/shared/`, converged **whole-set** to the canon
21	  head by the nightly refresh and stamped with its provenance. Propagation lags one nightly,
22	  lands as a reviewable commit on the member's `claudinite/maintenance` PR (auto-merged on
23	  `auto-merge` delivery once the repo's checks pass, held for the owner on `review`), and the
24	  rollback story is the same channel: fix the canon, the next nightly re-heals. A wrong
25	  *blocking* check still fails every member's Stop hook — visible and recoverable, but
26	  fleet-wide noise, so treat check changes as production changes.
27	- **Migration notes** (`engine/migrations/<date>-<slug>/`, or `packs/<pack>/migrations/<date>-<slug>/`) — the channel for anything convergence
28	  can't express: renames of consumer-held wiring, declaration rewrites, one-off agentic steps.
29	  Stamp-day-gated and idempotent; the note's `legacyPresent` telemetry says when the fleet has
30	  moved and (for `retire: 'auto'`) retires the record itself.
31	- **Copied artifacts** (pack `stubs/`, seeded configs) — these do **not** propagate at all. Each
32	  consumer holds its own copy, which drifts silently unless a check enforces its shape. Changing
33	  the source file alone only affects repos bootstrapped *after* the change.
34	- **Bootstrap wiring** (the committed artifacts [bootstrap.md](bootstrap.md) seeds:
35	  `settings.json` hook registrations, the two gitignore lines, the pack declaration) —
36	  propagates through the nightly update's idempotent backfills on the same delivery PR.
37	  The discipline: a change here is written as steps that **converge from every layout in the
38	  wild**, not just from the latest.
39	
40	Out-of-repo state remains the one channel git never reaches: a web environment's pasted Setup
41	script is snapshotted at environment build. A change that moves what the pasted script calls
42	needs the script's own probe to fail fast and a member issue asking for the one human action
43	(re-paste).
44	
45	## Migrating a copied artifact (stubs and the like)
46	
47	Because copies won't move on their own, we currently migrate them through the conformance
48	checks, in one Claudinite-only change:
49	
50	1. Change the source artifact in the pack (the stub under `packs/<pack>/stubs/`).

{"number":276,"title":"Move chrome-extension-release plumbing out of core `.github/` into the pack (vendored into consumers)","body":"Resolves the **RELEASE** item of #270: the reusable release workflows (`.github/workflows/chrome-extension-*.yml` + `deploy-privacy-page.yml`) and the three composite actions (`read-release-config`, `bump-extension-patch`, `report-failure`) live in Claudinite's core tree but exist solely for the `chrome-extension-release` pack. They must move behind the pack that owns them, leaving Claudinite with no release-specific GitHub Actions.

## Decision (agreed with owner)

- **Hosting model: vendor into each consumer.** GitHub only resolves reusable workflows/composite actions from a repo's own `.github/`, never from a `packs/…` subdir, so "into the pack" means the pack holds the templates and each consumer hosts a *managed* copy in its own `.github/`. Consumers become self-contained; baselining (not the consumer) owns keeping the copies correct. This reverses the original "thin consumer" design — deliberately.
- **Phase-2 deletion: automatic, telemetry-gated.** Once the fleet census confirms every consumer has vendored, the census deletes Claudinite's release plumbing automatically as part of migration retirement — no follow-up PR.
- **Secrets: nothing to migrate.** The four `CHROME_*` secrets already live in each consumer repo (they travel via `secrets: inherit` from the consumer's own workflow); Claudinite holds none.

## Plan

1. **Pack = source of truth.** Move the 4 workflows + 3 composite actions into `packs/chrome-extension-release/` as vendored templates; rewrite cross-repo `uses: missingbulb/Claudinite/.github/…@main` → local `uses: ./.github/…`; rename to avoid the in-repo filename collision (the orchestrator and the create-package reusable are both `chrome-extension-release.yml` today).
2. **Migration is the fix vehicle.** A new baseline migration carries: (a) a **materialize** op — baselining writes the vendored set into each consumer's `.github/` and drops the old thin-stub `@main` refs; (b) a **legacyPresent** probe ("still references `missingbulb/Claudinite/.github/workflows/chrome-extension-*`") for fleet telemetry; (c) a **retire-deletes-from-home** list — Claudinite's own release files. Extend the migration mechanism (today rename-only) with the materialize op, and teach the census to delete the home-repo files on retirement.
3. **Tolerant checks during transition.** The `cer/*` checks accept both the old thin-stub shape and the new vendored shape until the migration retires, so no consumer's check suite goes red mid-flight.
4. **Docs.** Update `RELEASE.md`, `.github/workflows/README.md` (drop the frozen-`@main`-API section), and the pack fingerprint.

## Prerequisite for the automatic cut

The automatic phase-2 deletion needs `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` granted **Contents-write on the home repo** — #239 notes this is not granted yet. Until it is, the census logs "grant FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN Contents write" and Claudinite's copies stay in place (harmless — consumers already run off their vendored copies by then).

{"number":748,"title":"conformance-backlog: committed-build-artifact check (promote cannot land a check — fixtures sit outside its write surface)","body":"Two things, from the 2026-08-11 `canon-curation/growth-promote` run (#745, PR #747).

## 1. A structural block: promote's ladder cannot reach the check rung

`growth-promote`'s task spec says a lesson a check can carry is **authored as the check** in the promote PR — "the rule module in the right pack, the failure message carrying the generalized lesson, **plus a fixture test proving it fires**".

That is mechanically impossible today:

- promote's write surface is bounded to `packs/` and `skills/`, enforced by `.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/promote-scope.mjs` on the `growth-promote` branch prefix;
- a canon pack's fixture test lives under `packs-tests/`, which is **outside** that surface;
- and it cannot move into `packs/` either — `.github/workflows/ci.yml` pins a closed set of test roots (`engine-tests/`, `packs-tests/`, `vendoring/`, `dev/tools/`, `.claudinite/local/packs/`), with `engine-tests/ci-test-roots.test.mjs` failing on any tracked test outside them.

So every promote run must fall back to prose for a convertible rule, and the "prose is the fallback, not the default" ladder never fires. Whichever way it is resolved (widen `inBounds` to `packs-tests/`, or add `packs/` as a test root), it is an owner decision — the run declined to widen its own gate.

## 2. The conversion this blocked

The `.gitignore`-pruning lesson (LaughCounter's local pack, promoted as prose to `git-github-advanced` in #747) converts to a world-scope `basics` check. Written and green locally before being pulled:

- **`packs/basics/committed-build-artifact.mjs`** — advisory, relevance-first. Flags a *tracked* file matching a confined set of artifacts no project tracks on purpose: `__pycache__/`, `*.py[co]`, `.pytest_cache/`, `.mypy_cache/`, `.ruff_cache/`, `*.egg-info/`, `.DS_Store`, `Thumbs.db`. The `fix` line carries the lesson (delete the artifacts before dropping their ignore rules; read `git diff --cached --stat` after a bulk `git add -A`).
- **`packs-tests/basics/committed-build-artifact.test.mjs`** — four cases: clean tree silent; a swept-in `__pycache__` found; the tool-cache/OS set found; and a narrowness case proving silence on deliberately vendored trees (`node_modules/`, `dist/`, `build/`) and on prose merely naming `__pycache__`.

Advisory rather than blocking on purpose: the fix is a deletion, and pre-existing junk in a member repo should surface as a finding to clear, not red that repo's sweep and block its maintenance PR.

The set was chosen so the check stays inert on anything a repo might legitimately vendor; `node_modules/` and `dist/` are deliberately excluded.

Refs #745.

{"number":409,"title":"Tracking-issue freshness: keep the plan issue in sync after every merge","body":"Implementation tracker for the tracking-issue freshness check. This issue is itself an instance of the pattern it tracks — it carries the live checklist; the committed doc carries the rationale.

**Read first (on `main`):**
- Design + plan — [`docs/tracking-issue-freshness/DESIGN.md`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/docs/tracking-issue-freshness/DESIGN.md)

**The problem:** a major task has two artifacts — a source-controlled design/migration plan and a GitHub tracking issue with a `- [ ]`/`- [x]` checklist (the "read status and pick up the work" point). When a phase lands, the committed plan's status is updated in the same PR (the diff forces review), but the issue checklist is a separate surface no diff touches, so it silently drifts. Already live: `per-project-scheduling/MIGRATION.md` says Phase 1 is "same day, no soak" while #394's Phase 1 item still says "Soak ~1 week."

**The design, in two surfaces:**
1. **In-session (timely):** a transcript-only post-merge check-the-work rule — `in-session-github-access` (blocking) means in-session code has no GitHub REST credential, so the rule reads the merge, the tracker discovery, and the post-merge checklist edit from the session transcript's MCP tool calls. Enablers: `work.mergedThisSession()` and a Stop-hook post-merge trigger (the merge recipe leaves a clean tree, which would otherwise fast-exit).
2. **Nightly (convergent):** plans state, per phase, *how completion is decided* — a checklist item may carry `` naming a dependency-free Node script whose **exit 0 means the phase is done** ("if this code passes, phase 3 is done"); no marker ⇒ the phase's prose **Verify** block in the plan doc is the criteria. The `plan-status-update` task (daily, gated on an open `plan-tracking` issue) re-derives every tracker's checklist from these verifiers — flipping what sessions missed, flagging (never auto-un-flipping) a checked item whose code verifier now fails.

**Invariant:** any open `plan-tracking` issue must carry a todo checklist and have a box **flipped** in the same session as each merge that advances it (after the merge, not before — an item isn't done until it's on `main`). The issue *count* is not enforced.

**Phases (detail in the design doc):**
- [ ] **Convention + seed** — define the `plan-tracking` label and its meaning in the `grow_with_claudinite` / merge docs; apply it to existing in-flight tracker(s) (#394).
- [ ] **Primitive + trigger** — `work.mergedThisSession()` (transcript-derived accepted PRs) and the Stop hook's post-merge trigger, each with red-first tests.
- [ ] **Verifier (in-session)** — the `plan-tracking-freshness` rule in `grow_with_claudinite`; fires when a merge happened with no post-merge checklist flip, quiet otherwise.
- [ ] **Recipe wiring** — `merge-to-main` gains the "sync the `plan-tracking` issue after the merge" step (prose asks; the check guarantees).
- [ ] **Docs** — the convention in the pack README; design-doc status box; this issue points at the doc.
- [ ] **Per-phase verifiers (convention)** — `` code verifiers (exit 0 ⇒ done) with prose Verify blocks as fallback; recorded in the pack README and the nightly worker doc.
- [ ] **Nightly status update** — the `plan-status-update` task (daily/sonnet/none, gated on an open `plan-tracking` issue): re-verifies each tracker, flips passes, flags regressions in a comment.

{"number":498,"title":"scheduler-workflow-shape should validate the scopes a repo's tasks actually need, not a fixed two","body":"Surfaced by the `growth-extract` run on #484, and pulled out of that run's RULES.md entries during review: this reads as a proposed mechanism change rather than a rule a session can follow, so filing it here instead.

## The gap

`packs/basics/scheduler-workflow-shape.mjs` validates exactly two permissions on a repo's `claudinite-scheduler.yml`, both hard-coded:

```
if (!/^\s*contents:\s*write\b/m.test(text))       → flag
if (!/^\s*pull-requests:\s*write\b/m.test(text))  → flag
```

Those two cover baselining's `deliver()` (push a branch, open a PR, arm auto-merge). They cover nothing a *task's worker* needs. So a task whose worker calls a GitHub endpoint requiring some third scope passes the check with a stub that never granted it, and the failure lands at runtime in a member repo.

## How it actually bit (#478)

`store-release`'s worker POSTs a `workflow_dispatch`, which needs `actions: write`. The stub granted `actions: read`. Every fire 403'd, the worker exited 1, and the scheduler converged the task to `needs-human` — leaving three cut-over members with no working release path. Nothing caught it earlier because nothing was looking: the check validates a fixed pair, and the next task needing a fourth scope will land exactly the same way.

## Suggested direction

Make the required scope set *derived* rather than fixed. Roughly:

1. Let a task declare what its worker needs in its `task.mjs` — e.g. `required_scopes: ['actions:write']` — alongside the existing `agent_model` / `expected_outcome` fields, validated by `task-contract.mjs`.
2. Have `scheduler-workflow-shape` union the declared scopes across the repo's enabled tasks with the baselining floor (`contents:write`, `pull-requests:write`) and assert the workflow grants each one, naming the task that needs it in the failure message.
3. Have the stub generator emit the union, so a repo that adopts a task gets the grant with it rather than hand-editing `engine/scheduler/stubs/claudinite-scheduler.yml`.

That turns "read the scope off the endpoint and grant it yourself, and hope you remembered" into a declaration the check enforces. Worth weighing against the simpler option — keep the check fixed but widen the floor to include `actions: write` — which costs a broader default token but no new contract surface.

Not started; opening for a decision on which direction (or neither) before any implementation.

1	# Usage fold — count skill loads and their denominators from the captured logs
2	
3	**This task runs no agent.** It is `agent_model: none` with `code-work: node worker.mjs`, so the whole pass is the deterministic [`worker.mjs`](worker.mjs) the executor runs as code-work, which calls its sibling in this folder, the counting and folding core ([`fold-usage.mjs`](fold-usage.mjs)). This file is the human-facing record of what that worker does; there is no agent phase.
4	
5	## What it does
6	
7	Daily: fetch this repo's orphan `conversation-logs` branch, count each capture file still inside the retention window, read the scheduler's own task-run records from its Actions logs since the last fold, and regenerate `.claudinite/local/usage.GENERATED.json` on a PR that lands itself where this repo's delivery settings allow (the shared landing helper, `engine/scheduler/land-pr.mjs`, owns those nuances — a `review` repo's PR waits for the owner). A byte-identical recompute opens nothing, and a repo with no logs branch yet still folds its task rows.
8	
9	What it counts, per bucket:
10	
11	- **`skillLoads`**, per skill name — `Skill` tool-use entries, plus user-typed `/command`s naming a skill this repo mounts (built-in CLI commands never match). Subagent streams included: a subagent loading a skill is a load.
12	- **`captures`** — capture events folded. **`merges`** — the subset with an issue behind them (issue `0` means none).
13	- **`sessions`** — distinct session ids; one session can capture more than once.
14	- **`userMessages`** — genuine human turns. **`userCommands`** — every typed `/command`.
15	- **`checks`**, per scope (`work` / `world`) — `runs` (observed activations), `failures` (runs that reported a blocking finding), `errors` (the runner could not launch), the `blocking`/`advisory` finding volume, and `ciRuns`/`ciFailures` (the CI subset of the first two). **`checkFindings`**, per rule id — which rule caught what.
16	
17	- **`tasks`**, per `pack/task` — **historical only.** These rows counted what the retired slot scheduler did with each due task (`agent`, `code_work`, `skipped`, `failed`, `deferred`). Nothing writes that record any more, so these rows stop growing as the last slot-era logs age out of Actions retention. The reader stays because the logs inside that window are still real; see "The task invocations are a census" below for what replaces it and what does not.
18	- **`taskExec`**, per `pack/task` — what the **agent session** did with the item it was handed, distilled from the captured conversation logs: `success`, `failed`, `task-gone` (the item named a task the repo no longer carries), `invalid`. Counted off the machine-readable `claudinite-task-exec` records the session prints (`record-exec.mjs`; format owned by `engine/scheduler/run-record.mjs`), deduped on the full record tuple per capture file — never scraped from the agent's prose. A sample, of the sessions that captured.
19	
20	The denominators are the point. A raw load count cannot tell healthy-rare from broken — a version-bump skill loading rarely is fine — so the question is loads *against the sessions where that skill's own declared trigger plausibly applied.*
21	
22	## The check failures are the win
23	
24	A skill load is evidence that guidance was *reached for*. A **check failure is evidence that it worked**: the finding goes back into the session through the Stop hook and the agent corrects before the work leaves the branch. So the failure counts are not a defect metric to drive down — they are the closest thing this pipeline has to a measure of what the corpus is worth, and `checkFindings` says which rule earned it.
25	
26	Neither runner writes a metrics file, so both are counted off the marks they already leave in the transcript, each read by one tested function against a fixture copied from a real capture:
27	
28	- **the Stop hook's `hooklog` line** (`… Stop: done exit=<n> <reason>`), which reaches the transcript via hook stderr — the only mark a *passing* run leaves, and therefore the only reason work-scope **runs** are countable and not just failures. Its reason also carries the two outcomes nothing else reveals: a `loop-guard-relent` (blocking findings that survived two fix attempts, printed as a message rather than a findings block) and a `runner-error` (the checks did not run at all — enforcement silently off, which is why it gets its own counter instead of hiding inside a clean day);
29	- **`report-findings`' summary line** (`N blocking, M advisory (<scope> scope: …)`), which names its own scope and survives the `| tail` an agent usually pipes a run through — printed only when there *were* findings, so it counts failures, never runs;
30	- **the runner's invocation in a Bash command** (`node …/check_the_world.mjs`), which is how the world scope runs at all — it is wired into the test/CI flow, not the Stop hook.
31	
32	Runs come only from the marks a passing run also leaves; where a runner ran without its command naming it (a `make test` wrapping it), the summary lines are the floor, so the count is the **max** of the two signals rather than their sum. Only Bash and CI-log tool results are read, paired back to the tool that produced them — in the corpus that owns the runners, reading a file that merely *mentions* this vocabulary is the ordinary case.
33	
34	### CI counts when the agent was in the loop on it
35	
36	Write, commit, let CI run, fix what it caught is the same correction loop as the Stop hook's, one turn wider — so a CI check failure the session acted on is the same kind of win. It counts exactly when the session **pulled the job log in**, which is what "the agent was in the loop" means operationally. A nightly or post-merge run nobody looked at stays uncounted, correctly: nothing was corrected.
37	
38	Two consequences, both mechanism rather than policy. Actions stamps every log line with its own timestamp before the command's output, so each mark tolerates that prefix — without it a fetched CI log reads as having printed nothing at all. And a job log gets fetched repeatedly while iterating on the failure, with nothing in a fetch saying *which run* it was, so CI texts dedupe on the check output itself: two fetches of one job collapse, two real runs differ by their timestamps.
39	
40	**Every check number is a floor.** A run whose CI log nobody fetched left no mark in any session transcript; neither did a hook killed before it logged; and a green CI sweep prints nothing to be seen by, which is why the CI share is carried separately as `ciRuns`/`ciFailures` instead of quietly skewing a rate. The under-count is one-directional by construction, which is what keeps "the checks caught N things this week" a claim worth making.
41	
42	## The task invocations were a census, and are not being replaced by one yet
43	
44	Everything above is read out of *sessions*, so it sees only what was captured. A whole half of what this repo does opens no session at all — a precondition that finds nothing to do, an agentless task whose whole work is its code-work, an item that yielded to another. None of that leaves a transcript, and the first of them is the most common thing scheduling does.
45	
46	The `tasks` rows used to answer that from the other side: the slot scheduler printed one line per due task into its own Actions log (`claudinite-task-run v1 <pack>/<task> [<slot>] <outcome>`), so every due task was counted whether or not anything captured. **That writer is gone with the slot scheduler**, and the queue does not print an equivalent — each occurrence's outcome now lives on its own work item, as an `outcome:*` label, which is a better record and a different read entirely.
47	
48	So read these rows as history: exact within the window they cover, ending where the slot scheduler did, and not comparable to a period after it. The reader is kept rather than deleted because the logs it reads are still inside Actions retention; when they age out it counts nothing, which is the correct answer rather than a fault. Restoring a live census from the queue's own labels is tracked in #994 — it is a new read, not a repair of this one.
49	
50	They are also the one family here that is **appended once rather than recomputed**, past a `runsFoldedThrough` watermark ([`read-task-runs.mjs`](read-task-runs.mjs)). The reason was the source: the capture files are a local git branch this fold re-reads for free, while the run logs are a rate-limited REST read at two calls per run, and re-reading the whole window nightly would cost ~20x the API calls for the same answer. The price is stated rather than hidden — a counting bug fixed later applies from the fix forward and does not heal these rows.
51	
52	## Two tiers, two different mechanisms
53	
54	- **Days** are recomputed **from scratch, every run**, from the live capture files. No ingest ledger, no double-count risk, and a counting-bug fix self-heals the whole visible window on its next run. A day row drops out when its raw files age past retention — its content lives on in its week row.
55	- **Weeks** are appended **once**, past a single `foldedThrough` watermark: every day that has closed since the mark is added to its ISO week and the mark advances. Days close strictly in order, so a monotone mark is the entire exactly-once mechanism.
56	
57	Week rows are frozen by that trade: a counting bug found later heals the day window automatically, but weeks folded under the old counting keep it — re-freezing would need raw data the retention TTL deliberately destroyed. Git history records which commit folded what. A *new* counter meets the same trade from the other end: weeks folded before the check counts existed carry no `checks` key, and the fold grows them from the day they close forward rather than refusing to advance the watermark past them — a partial series beats a wedged one.
58	
59	## The file is GENERATED
60	
61	`.claudinite/local/usage.GENERATED.json` is machine-written and never hand-edited — it lives under `.claudinite/local/` because that is the repo-owned area the vendoring refresh never touches. The worker also declares its `merge=ours` `.gitattributes` entry, so a conflicting merge resolves by re-running the fold rather than by hand.
62	
63	## Failure is visible, never silent
64	
65	A fold outage longer than about `retention_days - 1` days loses the raw backing for the unfolded days. That loss is **declared**: each week row records how many days it absorbed, so a week reading `days: 5` states its own hole rather than quietly reporting a smaller number as if it were complete.
66

{"number":883,"title":"queue engine: implement the work-as-work amendments (heartbeat, tick/drain decoupling, self-re-dispatch, durable record, readiness re-check at close, prework key rename)","body":"The work-as-work review (#876) landed in the design docs and the simulator; `engine/scheduler/queue/` still implements the pre-review contract. Until each box below lands, the design describes behavior the engine does not yet have:

- [ ] **Heartbeat comments** — the executor comments on the item every ~15 min during the work step (`prework-run.mjs` / `executor.mjs`); the tick's leash reclaim then measures heartbeat silence. While off: long work is illegal (the leash/timeout arithmetic caps runs under an hour) and items go dark during work.
- [ ] **Retire `timeout-minutes ≤ leash`** in both workflow comments once the heartbeat lands; size run timeouts to `maxItems` × the largest work bound. (DESIGN §6.)
- [ ] **Tick/drain decoupling** — the drain job must leave the cron workflow's `claudinite-tick` concurrency group (own group, or the executor workflow via dispatch). While off: a multi-hour drain starves the hourly tick (F19) — currently masked only by the 50m timeout the heartbeat retires.
- [ ] **Self-re-dispatch** — a drain exiting with ready items left `workflow_dispatch`es the executor workflow (`GITHUB_TOKEN` can fire it). While off: leftover items wait a tick each.

18	// reusables. The daily schedule is contract too: STUB_CRON pins every repo's

{"number":801,"title":"Migration to the work-item queue: two PRs, one same-day validation burst","body":"The phase plan for [tasks-dispatch DESIGN](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md) (§14 points here). Design constraints from the owner (2026-08-13): **fewest disparate steps, fewest approval points, and certainty the same day** — we do not wait for a nightly run to learn whether the end state works. Deliberately generating real work to push traffic through every path is explicitly sanctioned.

**Approval points: two.** PR‑1 (mechanism + canon flip) and PR‑2 (fleet flip + slot deletion). Everything else is forcing and observing, which the mechanism itself defines as ordinary operations.

Checkboxes track progress; each burst row's checkbox is checked only with an evidence URL appended beside it.

---

## Where this stands (2026-08-16 12:10Z)

**One member is verified end to end, agentic lane included. Twelve more are blocked on owner-only credential work.** Steps 0–2 complete. Step 3 is most of the way: the flip is merged and observed, the first member ran a real agentic item to `outcome:done`, and three defects the burst could not have caught were found and two fixed. The slot deletion still waits on the remaining members.

| | state |
|---|---|
| Canon | on the queue since #854; 12 clean scheduler runs overnight, 12 items to terminal state |
| Fleet | flipped by default in #888 (`17902b9`); **GCEC verified end to end**, 12 members still need a CCR routine (#916) |
| Slot machinery | still in the tree, deliberately — deleting it before members are verified strands them (see Step 3) |
| Design vs engine | DESIGN/sim current to §15.24 plus F24; engine at pre-review behavior — the catch-up is Step 4 (#883) |
| Open follow-ups | #916 (owner-only, blocking), #921, #892, #924, #883, #877 |

## Step 0 — rehearsal (done)

- [x] Simulator + scenario suite green in CI; coverage map names the live-only rows

## Step 1 — PR‑1 on canon: the whole mechanism, canon flipped (approval №1)

- [x] Label vocabulary, tick workflow (cron + `workflow_dispatch`), executor workflow, janitor re-target, dependency fields + `after` yield + `create-work-item`, F8 signal exclusions, canon flipped, gate green
- [x] **Approval №1: PR‑1 merged** — #854, `b30ef77`

## Step 2 — the validation burst (complete)

- [x] **B1 creation + first-item rule (S25):** [run 31899008771](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31899008771) — 12 items #860–#870, each `task:blocked` wearing its next anchor
- [x] **B2 the roll + reasons on record (S1′):** #860 — one ask, rolled to tomorrow, reason on the item, no comment spam
- [x] **B3 agentic happy path + real CCR invocation + records (S2):** #867 — wake → claim → hand-off with nonce → **live session in 31s** → result + exec record → `outcome:done`
- [x] **B4 agentless path end to end:** #859 — wake → executor in 2s → claim → prework → `outcome:done`, closed in 26s, no session
- [x] **B5 the chain + yield (S4/S23):** #863 — yielded while `core/update` was live ([run 31913047785](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31913047785)), then claimed and running the moment the upstream cleared; its work merged as #887
- [x] ~~**B6 hourly cadence**~~ — **dropped** (owner). `create-extractor` is `gcec/create-extractor` on GoogleCalendarEventCreator, the fleet's only hourly task; canon has none
- [x] ~~**B7 missing-secret posture**~~ — **folded into Step 3** (owner): every member reaches the flip with its endpoint token unset, so the posture happens on real traffic with no scaffolding
- [x] **B8 force-while-executing mutex (S15):** #871 — queued behind the executing twin, then got its own verdict on release
- [x] **B9 multi-executor lease (S7):** #873 — three overlapping executors, exactly one claim, one execution
- [x] **B10 follow-up fields (S17):** #872 — `Blocked-by` + `Not-before` created and held blocked by the tick
- [x] **B11 janitor leashes:** [run 31900490000](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31900490000) — 12 blocked/rolling items, zero escalations
- [x] **All burst rows green**

### What the burst caught that the rehearsal could not

Four defects, none of which any simulator would have produced. Three are fixed:

- **#879 → #881 (merged).** Hand-off appended a second `### Context` instead of replacing the first, splitting the item's binding scope while `instructions.md` says to read "the Context section", singular. Every unit test passed, because each tested one call. Confirmed fixed on live traffic in B5's own hand-off.
- **#882 → #885 (merged).** Queue sessions wrote `[unknown]` where the exec record's slot id used to go — `instructions.md` never said what replaces it — dropping the join from a record back to its work item.
- **The task-path guard fired correctly** on a hand-built item naming `task.mjs` instead of `task.md` (#871): refused, converged to `needs-human`, nothing run.
- **#892 (open).** The terminal convergence is agent-discretion, and **both** agentic runs got part of it wrong — #867's record field, and #863 closing with no outcome label and no exec record at all. Proposes a `converge-item.mjs` the session calls with its judged outcome.

## Step 3 — the fleet flip, then the deletion (approval №2)

**PR‑2 is two PRs, not one** (amendment, 2026-08-15). The plan said "slot machinery deleted in this same PR"; that is unsafe, and the reason is in the code:

- `updates/engine-update.mjs` **replaces the mount wholesale**, so a file canon deletes leaves every member's mount on its next converge whatever that member's config says.
- `.github/workflows/` is the one path a converge cannot push — staged, and landed later by the apply stage.
- The two stubs call **different entry points**: `run.mjs` vs `queue/tick.mjs`.

So deleting slots in the flip's own release strands any member whose workflow has not yet landed. Keeping the slot code makes that window benign (`run.mjs` no-ops) and #888 makes it **loud**.

- [x] The pack update flow staged only the scheduler workflow, so `claudinite-executor.yml` reached no member — #874, `5ca4c35`
- [x] **Approval №2: the flip merged** — #888, `17902b9`. `dispatchMode` answers `queue` for an absent setting, so members flip with **no edit to any file they own**
- [x] **A member's converge observed** — GoogleCalendarEventCreator, 2026-08-16 02:00:18–02:00:25Z: both stubs call the queue entry points out of the mount, `taskScheduler` carries no `dispatch` key, mount `queue/tick.mjs` byte-identical to canon HEAD, and [15 standing items created](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/918) (GCEC #904–#918). Last slot-era item was GCEC #903 at 00:09Z
- [x] **B7 lands here** — and the fault was **not** the unset secret the plan anticipated. `resolveEndpoint` fails at the *declaration*: [GCEC #908](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/908#issuecomment-5305803329) parked `needs-human` naming `taskScheduler.endpoints`, no session started. `endpoints` was declared in exactly one repo in the fleet — this one — so the flip left **every** member's agentic lane dark
- [x] **Per-member mini-burst on the first member (B1–B4 + B7 + B3 agentic)** — GCEC: agentless lane ran clean from 02:00Z; [GCEC #908 closed `outcome:done` at 11:28:16Z](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/908) via a live session started 11:16:12Z, its work landing as GCEC #923; [GCEC #907 `core/update`](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/907) closed `outcome:done` 11:49:02Z, converging the mount through the queue itself
- [ ] **The other 12 members wired and observed** — blocked on #916 (owner-only: one CCR routine + `CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN` per repo)
- [ ] #921 folded in — DESIGN §8's force recipe yields an item `pickOrder` can never pick
- [ ] **Then** the slot deletion PR (slots.mjs, run-ledger math, exclusive claim, re-arm, `FORCE_TASKS` path, slot-conformance checks)
- [ ] The migration reports itself through the mechanism it ships: per-member fan-out items + a fan-in item `Blocked-by` all of them (S18 live) — fan-in closed `outcome:done`

### What Step 3 caught that Step 2 could not

Three defects, each invisible to the burst for a specific reason — and the reasons are the finding:

- **#906 → #907 (merged).** `queue/instructions.md` was never in the vendor set: `computeVendorSet` drops every `engine/**/*.md` behind a two-entry operational whitelist, and #854 added a third operational doc without extending it. That file *is* the behavior of a work-item session. **Invisible because canon runs the engine from its repo root, not a mount** — so no amount of canon traffic could show it.
- **#922 → #925 (merged).** F18's episode boundary was stated semantically and implemented over only the paths that already wrote a comment; the roll and the `needs-human` park end an episode silently, leaving a claim that outranks every future claimant. The roll self-heals via the leash (canon #860 sat unrunnable 17:44Z→03:32Z); the park never does. Fixed by *striking* the claim — including on the **losing** claimant, whose claim would otherwise become the earliest of the next episode. **Invisible because the simulator modelled the rule's intent rather than its artifact**, so it was correct by construction; the sim now models the artifact and reproduces the bug without the fix.
- **#921 (open).** DESIGN §8's force recipe — strip `task:blocked`, optionally add `task:urgent` — omits `task:ready`, and `pickOrder` admits on `task:ready` alone. A forced item is invisible to every executor and the run logs `nothing ready to pick up`, which looks exactly like a healthy run. **Invisible because no executable artifact pins DESIGN's prose recipes.**

## Step 4 — the work-as-work engine catch-up (#883; starts only after Step 3's verification)

#884 (merged 2026-08-16, `4380639`) changed the design under the shipped mechanism — decisions §15.14–24. **The behavior-by-behavior checklist lives in #883** — one box per capability, each stating what breaks while it's off; this plan owns only the sequencing:

- [ ] **Step 4 waits for Step 3's per-member verification** — the flip wave must be observed on the engine it shipped, not one changing underneath it
- [ ] Each #883 behavior lands burst-style per this plan's own discipline: a forced run observed on canon the same day; the workflow-touching pieces (heartbeat, decoupling, continuation job, suspend-all) additionally observed on one member's converge before the fleet's
- [ ] #892's `converge-item.mjs` is the natural carrier for #883's durable-record box — land them together, not twice
- [ ] #924 (a losing claimant's comment defers the leash reclaim) rides #883's heartbeat, which introduces the per-holder liveness signal it needs
- [ ] #877 (the tick rename) unblocks when this step closes — last, so the rename never churns files mid-migration

## Done means

- [x] All Step‑2 rows have evidence URLs on this issue
- [x] The first member flipped, wired and observed end to end — agentless and agentic
- [ ] All members flipped and observed; fan-in item closed `outcome:done`
- [ ] Slot machinery gone from the tree
- [ ] Step 4: the fielded engine matches DESIGN §15.14–24 — #883 closed
- [ ] 48h of ordinary operation as *confirmation* — explicitly not the proof; the burst was the proof

Collapse packs-tests/ into packs/ — a pack's tests live inside the pack (#1070)

* Collapse packs-tests/ into packs/ — a pack's tests live inside the pack

Every packs-tests/<pack>/… file moves to packs/<pack>/…, beside the file it
covers, so the parallel tree that had to be kept mirroring packs/ by hand is
gone. The files that belonged to no pack go to the tree that owns them: the
fixture-consumer rehearsal to vendoring/, beside the converge it drives, and
the corpus-wide tests (pack-directory, pack-versions, manual-task-preconditions,
rule-index) to engine-tests/, which is already where the canon's whole-repo
tests live when no pack owns them.

Members see nothing. compute-vendor-set already drops *.test.mjs on the way
into a mount, so the computed set — files, engine version, pack versions — is
byte-identical to before the move, and no pack version changes. That is now
asserted over the real corpus rather than only a fixture: a fixture spelling
the *.test.mjs rule cannot notice the day it stops selecting the real tree.

Three places assumed tests were somewhere else and are corrected rather than
worked around: the dashboard's member fixture now copies its pack the way the
vendor set lays it down, sheepdog's permission-list guard takes a test naming
the permissions it asserts on as out of scope, and the engine/pack-lane shim
guard no longer counts a test's engine import as fielded.

Refs #1066

* Stop the four shipping files that cited a test from citing one at all

The move deleted the packs-tests/ paths four pack files named in comments. The
owner's call on the fork is that production code should not reference its tests
at any path, so the citations go rather than get repointed: each note keeps what
it was saying — the duplication is deliberate, a drift guard pins the copies —
and names the guard instead of its file.

That is a content change in three pack directories, and the delivery signal is
the pack version, so chrome-extension, claudinite-lifecycle and sheepdog bump.
It is the one place "no version change" could not hold: a comment pointing at a
tree that no longer exists is not something to leave shipped.

pack-version-bumped no longer counts a pack's tests, for the reason the vendor
set does not carry them — nobody is waiting on a file nothing delivers, and a
bump for one would re-deliver every pack in the tree to say nothing.

Refs #1066

---------

{"number":1066,"title":"Collapse packs-tests/ into packs/ — a pack's tests live inside the pack","body":"A pack's tests sit in a parallel tree (`packs-tests//…`) that has to be kept mirroring `packs//…` by hand. Co-locate them: each test lands beside the file it covers, inside its pack.

## Constraint

**Zero change in what any member repo sees.** The vendor set must come out byte-identical, so no pack version changes and no member converge notices anything. `compute-vendor-set.mjs` already drops `*.test.mjs` from the walk, so co-located tests are excluded by the rule that is already there — this is verified by diffing the computed set (all canon packs declared) before and after.

## Scope

- `packs-tests//**` → `packs//**`, mirroring the existing structure.
- The files that belong to no pack move to the tree that owns them:
  - `packs-tests/rehearsal/` (fixture consumers + the converge runner) → `vendoring/rehearsal/`, beside the vendor computer/writer it drives.
  - `pack-directory`, `pack-versions`, `manual-task-preconditions`, `rule-index` → `engine-tests/`, which is already where the canon's whole-repo tests live (`ci-test-roots.test.mjs`, `migrations.test.mjs`) when no pack owns them.
- CI's test-root list, the `ci-test-roots` drift guard, and every doc/comment naming `packs-tests/`.

## Outcome

Landed as #1070. The file set is byte-identical as intended. Three pack versions did move, and deliberately: four shipping files carried comments citing `packs-tests/…` paths this change deletes, and the call on that fork was that production code should not reference its tests at any path — so the citations were removed, which is a content change in `chrome-extension`, `claudinite-lifecycle` and `sheepdog`.

The general form of that rule, and the eleven pre-existing sites it still has to clean, is #1072.

{"number":564,"title":"Pack manifests as JSON: pack.json + pack.schema.json, code split into sibling files","body":"Owner comment (process-change): "Why are packs declared using mjs? Is it just the `detect` part? It seems they can all be just JSON declarations, and if we have some code that detects, we can put that in a different file. And once it's just JSON — can't you declare the schema in a nicer way than `engine/pack_loader/pack-schema.mjs`? You can still have validations (a simple unit test) for making sure all the skills/rules are declared and there's no drift, but at least the files will be sane."

Measured across the 29 manifests (27 canon + the home's 2 local packs): **988 lines, 56 of them `import` statements, 350 of them comments.** Almost nothing in a `pack.mjs` needs to be code.

## What is actually code today

| Field | Packs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `detect` | 13 (14 declare `null`) | ~10 are one-liners over `ctx.tracked` — `includes`, `endsWith`, a path regex, or the shared `hasMarkerNearRoot` helper — all expressible as data. **3 need real logic**: `chrome-extension` (locates the extension manifest), `chrome-extension-release` (recognizes a release orchestrator workflow), `leaflet` (scans file *content*). |
| `worldRules` / `workRules` | all | Code only as *imports*. In JSON these become filenames the loader imports. |
| `env` | 2 | Genuinely code — `setup`/`probe` are functions of the pack's config returning shell. |
| `contributes` / `contributedRules` | 3 / 1 | `contributes` is a map of pack id → rule modules, so filenames. `contributedRules` (barriers only) is a real seam. |
| everything else | — | Pure data: `id`, `badge`, `marker`, `prose`, `seededByDefault`, `requires`, `ruleRoutingGuidance`, `skills`, `questions`. |

## Shape wanted

- `packs//pack.json` for all 29, with `$schema` pointing at a `pack.schema.json`.
- Optional sibling code files, named from the JSON, only where needed: `detect.mjs` (3 packs), `env.mjs` (2), `contributed-rules.mjs` (1).
- Rules referenced **by filename**, which buys a drift guard the current shape cannot have: every rule `.mjs` in the pack directory must appear in exactly one of the two scope lists. Today an undeclared rule module is simply invisible.

## Why it is worth more than tidiness

**The loader stops executing arbitrary code at load.** Today a consumer's local `pack.mjs` is `import()`ed during SessionStart in every session and on every check run — which is precisely why `pack-registry.mjs` carries per-pack import isolation. With JSON, the ~26 packs that need no code execute none.

**A real schema.** `pack.schema.json` gives editor autocomplete and validation that `PACK_FIELDS` never will.

## What it costs

1. **The 350 comment lines have nowhere to go** — and they are real rationale, not noise: why `basics` requires `barriers` and contributes the isolation barrier as manifest data, why `canon-curation`'s declaration cardinality is what makes its tasks central-once. The natural home is the pack README, which is now exactly the "rationale the manifest cannot carry" file after #559 — this brings two or three of the deleted ones back.
2. **`pack.mjs` is a consumer-held shape**, not only ours — every member repo has local packs. Needs both-shapes tolerance plus a baseline migration to retire the old one, per `consumer-safe-changes.md`.

## Scope note on validation

A consumer's local pack must be validated at *their* Stop hook, not this repo's CI, so loader-side validation stays. JSON Schema replaces the **field-shape** half of `pack-schema.mjs`; the **cross-file drift guards** (skills ↔ directory, rules ↔ files) remain loader checks with unit tests over them. Net effect: that module shrinks substantially rather than disappearing.

# Website release flows — alignment design

Status: **proposed** (owner review pending). Refs #722.
Inputs: [COMPARISON.md](COMPARISON.md) (the fleet evidence), [SOUNDNESS.md](SOUNDNESS.md)
(the independent soundness analysis). The subject is the `static-website` pack — merged in
#611 — and the three site repos' bespoke flows it is meant to replace.

> **State note (2026-08-09, evening).** After this design was written, canon merged #729
> (`build_vars`) and EdFringeNow adopted the pack (#319) — see the state updates in
> COMPARISON.md and SOUNDNESS.md. Per the owner's instruction, that movement is treated
> as *data, not as the desired outcome*: this design's conclusions stand where they
> disagree with what shipped. Decisions affected by the new state say so inline.

## Goal

One github-pages-serving standard, owned by the pack, with:

- **no bespoke release mechanism left in any site repo** — the bespoke deploy workflows,
  bump scripts and CI variants all go;
- **minimum GitHub Actions surface** — YAML only where the platform forces it (triggers,
  permissions, OIDC, the Pages actions); all logic in scripts the ordinary vendoring
  converges. The rule of thumb the owner stated holds: a step that needs a secret or the
  repo token must run in Actions; nothing else has to;
- **minimum manual repo settings** — a fresh repo that declares the pack releases on the
  first push, with the custom domain as the only genuinely manual item;
- **customization without forks** — everything repo-specific in `.github/site.config`;
  the workflows stay copy-verbatim.

The acceptance probe (owner-specified): purge every release-related aspect *and setting*
from MissingBulbWebsite so it simulates a new repo, adopt the pack, and the first release
must work on the first go.

## Decisions

### D1. Keep one pack; reshape `static-website` in place

The consolidation policy survives the soundness review intact — one vendored standard,
repo-specifics in a small explicit config. The pack is reworked in place; with EdFringeNow
now adopted (#319), the reshape carries one live adopter's vendored copies along — a
normal converge plus one agent-stage handoff for its workflow files, small and bounded,

# Task dispatch without slots — the work-item queue

The mechanism lives in [`engine/scheduler/queue/`](../../engine/scheduler/queue/),
behind `taskScheduler.dispatch`. A continuation of the owner's sketch (2026-08-12, reproduced in Appendix A), played against twenty timed
scenarios ([SCENARIOS.md](SCENARIOS.md)) and the field's prior art
([RESEARCH.md](RESEARCH.md)), with the owner's eight decisions of 2026-08-13
recorded in §15 and folded into the sections they changed. The phase plan
belongs to a tracking issue, not here. It supersedes
the slot machinery of
[per-project-scheduling DESIGN §3–§5](../per-project-scheduling/DESIGN.md) and
amends several of its §12 decisions (each amendment is named where it happens).
What it does **not** touch: the task folder anatomy (§1), the precondition
contract, code-work and its secrets model
([task-code-work DESIGN](../task-code-work/DESIGN.md)), the outcome ceiling, the
security posture (the issue is data; behavior comes from tracked files), and the
usage-metrics records.

The shape in one paragraph: **work items are issues, available for work; any
number of executors pull from them.** A thin generator tick gives every
recurring task a standing work item at its anchor and flips blocked items
ready — pure label mechanics, no preconditions, no signals. An executor — a
GitHub Action by default, but anything that can read issues — picks up the
next ready item, claims it by label, evaluates the precondition (the only
place it ever runs): on a go it runs the work step and hands off to agentic work (a
CCR session invoked by API); on a no-go the item **rolls** — stamped
not-before the task's next anchor, blocked, reason recorded — so the item
itself carries "asked, declined, wakes at T". Follow-ups, fan-outs, urgency,
and one-off forcing are all just *creating or waking work items*. There is no
slot id, no run-ledger watermark, no exclusive claim, and no label-event
re-arm.

---

## 1. What the slot machinery costs today

The current design is push-shaped: one hourly scheduler run decides, at a single
instant, everything that will happen — which tasks are due, whether they run,
what they may touch — and encodes the decision into dispatch issues that a
label-event-triggered session then executes. Every complication below is a
consequence of that shape.

- **The slot id is state smuggled into a title token.** `d2026-08-12`,
  `h2026-08-12T14Z`, `m2026-08` exist so that a scheduled occurrence has an
  identity — which the exactly-once guard needs (title search per slot), the
  stale backstop needs (the *leading character* of the slot id is parsed back
  into a period, `SLOT_PERIOD_MS`), and forcing needs (the `~f<runId>` marker
  appended so an operator re-run of an already-run slot isn't silently
  swallowed). Three mechanisms each decode a fragment of scheduler state out of
  a string in an issue title.

- **Due-ness lives in a platform side channel.** "Has this slot run?" is
  answered by the Actions run ledger of the scheduler workflow itself
  (`lastSuccessTime`) — a watermark that is not visible beside the work, must
  exclude forced runs to stay correct, and whose unreadability has to fail the
  whole run (an exit-0 abort would advance it past slots it never evaluated).
  The state the system actually cares about — *was this occurrence's work
  created?* — is derivable from the issues themselves, and nothing reads it
  from there. *(A first cut of the go/no-go ruling briefly reintroduced a
  ledger read; the standing-item model (§5) removed it again — the tick is
  now a pure function of the clock and the issue list.)*

# Claudinite work-item queue — the generator tick and its drain (tasks-dispatch
# DESIGN §5, §10). This is the repo's ONLY cron, and it replaces the slot
# scheduler's content at the same path when `taskScheduler.dispatch` is `"queue"`
# — same file, same hashed minute, different mechanism, so the one-cron rule and
# every reader that knows this workflow by name keep holding.
#
# A thin shim: all logic lives in the vendored engine, so this file changes
# rarely. The minute below is a placeholder; bootstrap and the wiring converge
# rewrite it to this repo's stable hashed minute in :10–:50, computed by
# `node engine/scheduler/hash-minute.mjs <owner/repo>`.
#
# TWO JOBS, IN ORDER. The tick is pure label mechanics over the issue list —
# instantiate each task's standing item at its anchor, ready what is due, reclaim
# dead executor claims — and evaluates no precondition and collects no signal. The
# drain is an ordinary executor run: it picks up what the tick just created, which
# is what keeps the common case's latency at zero even with no `labeled` event
# delivered. Lost events are therefore never the only delivery — they are latency
# sugar, which is what retires the re-arm.
#
# `workflow_dispatch` is not a convenience: it is the never-wait-for-the-cron
# lever every forced run, migration and validation burst depends on. Its one
# input is how that lever reaches ACROSS repos: the fleet enforcer dispatches
# this workflow naming the tasks to run now, and this member wakes its own
# standing items with its own token (DESIGN §8). The alternative — the enforcer
# editing every member's issues directly — would widen the fleet PAT to issue
# writes on every repository, for a job the member can do for itself.
name: Claudinite scheduler

on:
  schedule:
